| Internal identity | botmux injects session, owner and other internal variables last; `BOTMUX*`, `__OWNER_OPEN_ID`, `CODEX_HOME` and the like can't be forged through `env` or `inherit` |

Adapter variables such as `TRAE_HOME` and `CLI_EXTRA_ARGS` aren't inherited automatically in strict mode either; list them in `inherit` or set them in `env` if you need them.

How to set it:

* Dashboard: "Inherit host environment" above "Bot Config → Advanced → Launch environment → Session environment".
* CLI: `botmux env-policy set '{"mode":"strict","inherit":["HTTPS_PROXY"]}'` (pick the bot with `--bot`); `unset` restores the default.
* Feishu: `/botconfig set envPolicy {"mode":"strict"}`.

Bad formats, unknown fields and reserved names are rejected outright, never silently downgraded.

**When it applies**: on the next cold start of a session. Offline CLI edits only change the file; the daemon reads it on its next start. When the daemon restarts and restores sessions whose policy no longer matches, it closes the old session first and starts fresh; if it can't confirm the old one is gone, it refuses to start. Environment a CLI has already read can't be revoked.

**Coverage**: strict mode covers PTY, tmux, zellij and zmx sessions started by botmux, plus local Codex / TraeX App Servers and helper processes such as title generation. tmux / zellij no longer load the `launchShell` startup files and launch the CLI with a clean environment, so PATH, nvm, mise and the like must come from the baseline or your explicit config. `TERM` defaults to `xterm-256color` when missing.

**Not supported**: Herdr, Riff, Mojo, Forge launch mode, adopted external processes and external App Servers can't provide the same isolation yet; strict mode refuses them. Config and credential files the CLI reads itself, file permissions and cloud accounts are outside this policy.

**With a network policy**: if `sandboxNetworkPolicy` is also set, proxy variables (`HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY` and lowercase forms) must also satisfy the table below. Strict inheritance only decides whether a variable reaches the CLI; it doesn't grant network access.

| Network config | Proxy variables |
| --- | --- |
| No network policy; or `proxyMode` unset and both public and private are `allow` | Not rejected by the network policy; in strict mode they still need to be listed in `inherit` or set in `env` |
| `proxyMode` unset and either zone is `block` / `allowlist` / `denylist` | Any non-empty proxy value refuses to start |
| `proxyMode: "reject"` | Any non-empty proxy value refuses to start |
| `proxyMode: "trusted-egress"` | Explicitly allowed proxies may stay; network rules must allow the proxy's IP and port, and the final targets are governed by the proxy's own ACL |

General proxy delegation in this table applies only to ordinary sessions. A frozen protected HTTP egress policy explicitly rejects `trusted-egress` and task proxy variables; adding that mode repeatedly cannot resolve the error. Model connections must use the protected model bridge, currently supported only by Codex. See [network sandbox documentation](/botmux/en/sandbox.md).

`trusted-egress` neither creates a proxy, grants environment variables nor guarantees the CLI uses it. Authorizing an exit does not restrict destinations behind it. If a model requires a proxy, do not simply remove its `inherit` grant to pass validation: explicitly trust the exit and configure endpoint rules plus deployment-layer ACLs, or first establish direct model authentication, permitted destination CIDRs/ports and DNS. Persistent backends such as tmux, adopt and external App Servers remain rejected regardless of `trusted-egress` or `envPolicy`.

The network policy itself requires Linux, the local PTY backend and `sandbox: "oncall"`. See [File and network sandbox](/botmux/en/sandbox.md).

## Auto-maintained fields (don't edit)

botmux writes these itself. They're listed here so you can read the file:

| Field | Description |
|------|------|
| `defaultOncallAutoboundChats` | Groups already auto-bound by `defaultOncall`. Once recorded, a group is never auto-bound again, even after unbinding |
| `noCardChats` | Groups where `/card off` turned off the live card |
| `noPinStreamingCardChats` | Groups where `/card pin off` turned off live card pinning |
| `noCotChats` | Groups where `/cot off` turned off the thinking message |
| `chatReplyModes` / `chatMentionModes` | Per-group settings written by `/reply-mode` and `/mention-mode` |

### Grant store (`grants.sqlite`) {#grant-store}

Per-person talk grants are not kept in `bots.json` but in `<data dir>/grants.sqlite` (default `~/.botmux/data/grants.sqlite`): `chatGrants`, `globalGrants`, and their message quotas and expiry. This keeps `bots.json` from growing every time several bots create a group together.

* At daemon startup, if `bots.json` still has these fields (left from before an upgrade, or written by hand), they're merged into the grant store and removed from `bots.json`; for the same entry the store wins. Before the first removal, the whole `bots.json` is backed up as `bots.json.bak-grants-v1`.
* Grants are only reclaimed automatically when they **expire**: at daemon startup and every hour after. To revoke early use `/revoke` or the grant card.
* In multi-replica mode (`BOTMUX_COORDINATION_MODE=primary`) grants stay in `bots.json`. Don't switch back and forth between modes: after switching to primary, grants in the grant store are not read.



---
url: /botmux/en/cards.md
---

# Streaming Cards

<video src="../img/video-v2-daily-en.mp4" controls preload="metadata" style="width:100%;border-radius:8px"></video>

Botmux uses Lark cards to show what the CLI is doing, and lets you control it right from your phone. This page goes from most common to advanced: first what shows up during a turn, then the status card, dynamic single cards and the switches, and finally the features for scripts and integrators.

## What shows up in the chat during a turn

| Layer | What it is | How to turn it off |
|-------|------------|--------------------|
| **Terminal status card** | One card per turn with a live terminal screenshot and session controls | Bot-level `disableStreamingCard`, or `/card off` in this chat |
| **Thinking process (CoT)** | The CLI's thinking text and tool calls, streamed as a native Lark CoT message | Bot-level `cotEnabled: false`, or `/cot off` in this chat |
| **Message status marks** | Only in chats with the status card off: a "GoGoGo" reaction on your message when work starts, swapped for ✅ when it ends | Bot-level `silentTurnReactions: true` |
| **Replies** | Answers, images, files and cards the agent sends with `botmux send` | Sent on demand, no switch |

A few notes:

* Status marks and the status card are **either/or**: with the status card on, no reactions are added; with it off, the reaction is the only lightweight progress signal. Swap the two emoji with `receivedReactionEmoji` / `doneReactionEmoji` (see [bots.json](/botmux/en/bots-json.md)).
* The thinking process needs Lark PC ≥ 7.70 or mobile ≥ 7.74, and only appears for CLIs that emit thinking (Claude Code, Codex, TraeX, Pi and others).
* To get "one card per turn" instead, see the "Dynamic single cards" section below.

## Terminal status card

![Streaming card](https://magic-builder.tos-cn-beijing.volces.com/uploads/1780419090587_img_v3_0212a_553ca347-4a93-491f-a2ef-30d00a374cdg.jpg)

The card body is a **live screenshot** of the terminal: xterm renders the CLI's interface in the background as an image (borders and colors included), instead of converting output to text.

### The header color is the status

| Status | Color | When |
|--------|-------|------|
| Starting… | Yellow | The CLI is still starting |
| Working | Blue | The turn is in progress |
| Analyzing… | Purple | Analysis in progress |
| Awaiting input / ✓ Turn ended · Awaiting input | Green | The turn is done; send the next message |
| ✓ Turn ended (AI determined no reply was needed) · Awaiting input | Green | The AI decided this turn needs no answer; see below |
| ⏳ Main turn ended · background tasks running (N) | Light blue | The main agent has answered, but background work it started (background agents, `run_in_background` Bash, Monitor, Grok background tasks) is still running; N matches the web terminal, and the turn only counts as done once all of it finishes |
| No recent progress | Red | No progress seen for a long time |
| Limit reached | Red | The model quota is used up; turns green "Ready to retry" once a retry is possible |
| Interrupted | Orange | The turn was interrupted |

### "No reply needed" and timing {#no-reply-needed}

* **No reply needed**: when the AI decides a message needs no answer (say, a status line someone posted in the group), no reply card is sent and the status card header reads "✓ Turn ended (AI determined no reply was needed) · Awaiting input", so you can tell it apart from a stuck turn. Automatic, nothing to configure. If the message explicitly @mentioned the bot, an automatic receipt is posted too; to force an answer, @mention it again and ask for a reply explicitly.
* **Waiting / execution time**: off by default; see [Showing timing](#showing-timing) below to turn it on.

### Card buttons

| Button | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| 📖 Show Output / 📕 Hide Output | Expand or collapse the terminal screenshot; when expanded you also get 📝 Export Text and 🔃 Refresh |
| 🖥️ Open Web Terminal | **Read-only** terminal view |
| 🔑 Get Write Link | Get a **writable** terminal link. Flat groups first try a "visible only to you" card; topics, private chats, or a failed send fall back to a DM |
| 🗜️ Compact | Send `/compact` to the CLI to compress context (shown only when the CLI supports it) |
| ⏲️ Idle auto-compact: on/off | Compact automatically after the session sits idle, same as [`/idlecompact`](/botmux/en/slash-commands.md) |
| ⏹ Stop | Interrupt the current turn (same as ^C); the session stays. Only shown while the turn is still running |
| ❌ Close Session | Close the session; adopted sessions show "⏏ Disconnect" here |
| 🔁 Retry Last Task | Appears when the quota recovers and the status becomes "Ready to retry" |
| Reasoning effort dropdown | Codex sessions (tmux backend, no sandbox, not using RPC input) can change reasoning effort while running; it applies from the next turn |

You can hide buttons you don't need in the Dashboard (see "Hiding card buttons" below).

### Interrupting or correcting a turn

**You don't have to wait for it to finish.** With output shown, the bottom of the card has quick keys: Esc, ^C, Tab, Space, Enter, arrow keys, ⇞ Page ½ Up, ⇟ Page ½ Down. Tapping Esc presses Esc in the terminal; after interrupting, just send a new instruction.

* The quick keys only appear when **output is shown**, and remote backends (Riff / Mojo) don't have them.
* By default, messages you send while a turn is running are queued and fed in after it ends. To correct course immediately, tap Esc or ⏹ Stop first.

### Card lifecycle

* **A new card each turn**: the previous card freezes as an archive, so history stays easy to follow. After a session is moved to another chat with [`/relay`](/botmux/en/relay.md), the original card also freezes and loses its buttons.
* **Resumable after close**: the close card has a "▶️ Resume Session" button. When the CLI supports native resume, it also shows the native command (e.g. `claude --resume <id>`) for manual recovery.
* Management buttons such as "🔄 Restart" live on the session card, not on each turn's status card.

## Cards that need a click from you

Besides the status card, Botmux posts cards when it needs you to decide something. These three are the most common.

### Repo picker card

When a new topic needs a repo, a "📁 Project Repository" card appears: pick a repo from the dropdown, type any directory by hand, or press "▶️ Start Session Directly" to use the default directory.

To open a new worktree from a repo, use the "🌿 Open a repo as a new worktree" dropdown. When 2 or more repos are found, a "🔀 Multi-repo" button sits next to it:

* Press it to switch to the **multi-repo picker**, where you can tick several repos and get one worktree each; press "🔀 Single-repo" to switch back.
* The switch is written to the bot setting `worktreeMultiPicker`, so it **applies to all of this bot's future sessions**, not just this card. That's why only admins can press it.
* You can also set it directly: `/botconfig set worktreeMultiPicker on|off`.

### AI question cards

When the agent asks with `botmux ask`, or Claude Code / Codex asks a question on its own, a question card appears in the chat. Its "Can answer" field tells you who can answer.

| What you see | What to do |
|--------------|------------|
| Single / multiple choice | Press an option; for multi-select pick as many as you like, then press "Submit". Submitting with nothing selected needs a second "Confirm empty submit" |
| Several questions on one card | Each is labeled "Question 1", "Question 2", ...; answer them all, then "Submit" once |
| Text / number fields | Fill them in; required fields can't be blank, and numbers must stay within any given range |
| Options already selected | These are the asker's recommended defaults, only a draft. Nothing counts as an answer until you press "Submit", and you can change them |
| "Other / custom answer" | Most questions have their own input box (unless the asker turned it off, or the card has text / number fields). Write your own answer when no option fits; it replaces only that question. Up to 1000 characters per question, 2000 per card |
| "Can answer" @-mentions one person | The asker named an answerer with `--answerer`, and only that person can submit (questions routed in from another app show "designated member only" instead). It only limits who can answer; it is not a business approval |

Without a designated answerer, anyone in the chat who can talk to the bot can answer. If no option fits, you can also just reply in the topic with text. See [CLI commands](/botmux/en/cli-commands.md) for the flags.

### Terminal permission card (Claude Code)

Some Claude Code actions pop a confirmation dialog in the terminal, for example a risky `rm` caught by a built-in safety check, which appears even when permission prompts are skipped. Lark can't see that dialog, so the session would hang. Botmux turns it into a question card showing the tool name and the command or file path, with buttons labeled 「允许执行」 (allow) and 「拒绝」 (deny). The card text and buttons are currently Chinese only.

* Allow lets Claude run it; deny tells Claude no, and it continues another way.
* It **waits 10 minutes by default**. If no one presses anything, it counts as denied and Claude is told it timed out.
* A text reply in the topic also counts as **denied**; your words are passed to Claude as the reason.
* If the card can't be delivered (for example, the daemon is unreachable), it is denied too, instead of falling back to a terminal dialog no one can press.
* Change the wait with the environment variable `BOTMUX_PERMISSION_TIMEOUT_MS` (milliseconds). It is clamped to between 1 second and 14 minutes (see [Environment variables](/botmux/en/env.md)).

## Dynamic single cards: one reply card per turn (preview)

![Dynamic single card illustration: in progress and finished](/img/unified-reply-card-preview.png)

The image is an illustration (in Chinese); the real look follows the Lark client.

By default, the status card, the thinking process and the final answer are separate messages. **Dynamic single card mode** puts the turn's progress, process, questions and final answer into one card that updates in place; the next turn starts a new card, and the previous answer stays.

### Turning it on

* Dashboard: Bot config → Task Cards → **Reply presentation**, choose "Dynamic single card".
* Or an admin sends in a chat: `/botconfig set replyCardMode unified`; switch back with `/botconfig set replyCardMode legacy`.
* It takes effect from the **next turn**.

Want only one card? Choose dynamic single card and turn off "**Show a separate status card**" (on by default). The terminal status card is then no longer posted automatically while the reply card keeps updating; use `/card` to open one when you need it. `disableStreamingCard` and `/card off` also turn off this separate status card. The old `final-only` value is treated as "dynamic single card + separate status card off".

### Which sessions are supported

* Supported: ordinary Lark conversations with Claude Code, Codex, Grok, TraeX and Pi **without a file sandbox** (both regular groups and topics).
* Not supported, still using the default mode: file-sandbox sessions (including `readIsolation` and global `BOTMUX_SANDBOX=1`), API-only, non-Lark channels, remote Riff/Mojo, adopt, local terminal sync, doc comments, video meetings, scheduled tasks, and v3 workflows.
* Sandbox state is fixed when the session starts; changing the bot's sandbox switch does not affect running sessions.

### What the card contains

* **Title**: the current phase plus elapsed time, such as ⏳ Queued, 💭 Working, ✅ Completed, ❌ Failed, ⏹ Stopped; while a question is pending it shows "Waiting for your response".
* **Process**: thinking text or summaries the CLI emitted, tool calls, progress notes and Q\&A records in order, folded into a 📋 section when the turn ends. Internal thinking the CLI never printed cannot be shown.
  * `/cot off` in the chat or bot-level `cotEnabled: false` hides the process; progress and Q\&A records stay.
  * To hide only tool calls: turn off "Show tool calls" in the Dashboard, or `/botconfig set replyCardShowTools off`. Thinking summaries and progress still show, and `/cot show` won't reveal hidden tools. This switch only applies to dynamic single cards.
* **⏹ Stop**: also on the reply card while it runs; it only stops the current turn, and an old card cannot stop a new task. Codex RPC input mode has no Stop button.
* **Width**: adapts to the chat window.

### Questions (Ask) live in the card too

`botmux ask` in the same turn, and Claude Code / Codex questions, open right inside the reply card with a "Waiting for your response" title. Once answered, timed out or expired, they fold into the process; multiple questions show one after another without overwriting each other. Multi-select, text answers and answering from the Dashboard all work as usual.

Large forms with more than 16 options or question content over 3000 bytes are still sent as separate cards. Approval / authorization cards are also sent separately.

### Working with `botmux send`

* `botmux send` counts as progress by default; send the final answer with `botmux send --response-kind final "full answer"`.
* Repeated sends may return the same `messageId`. If a script needs a separate message each time, use the default mode or `--response-kind auxiliary`.
* Replying with an @ to this turn's asker (`--mention-back`) still updates the same card; mentioning others, custom cards, images and files, and cross-session delivery are sent separately.

### Limits

* The whole card is bound by Lark's 30 KB update limit. Only when it is exceeded is the process truncated, keeping the final answer and pending questions first, with a note on how much was omitted.
* Very long answers become a Markdown attachment, with a note in the card.
* A withdrawn card is not rebuilt automatically; there is no typewriter animation.

## Switches at a glance

### Bot-level defaults vs per-chat overrides

| Layer | Bot-level default (Dashboard "Bot config → Task Cards") | Per-chat override (send in the chat) | Default |
|-------|---------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|---------|
| Separate status card | `disableStreamingCard` | `/card off` / `/card on`; bare `/card` summons one now | On |
| Thinking process | `cotEnabled` | `/cot off` / `/cot on`; `/cot show` for one look; `/cot` shows status | On |
| Message status marks | `silentTurnReactions` | None | Automatic in card-off chats; `true` stops them |
| Card buttons | `hiddenStreamingCardButtons` | None | All shown |
| Pin status card | `pinStreamingCard` | `/card pin off｜on｜status` | Off |

* Per-chat settings win over the bot-level default and only affect that chat. `/card on` only clears the chat-level off; a bot-level off still applies.
* **`/card` and `/cot` are admin-only (`allowedUsers`)**, status queries included. Lark cards can't show different views to different people, so one change affects everyone in the chat.
* `silentTurnReactions` also hides Codex App's "follow-up instruction received" receipt.

**Quiet preset**: one click in the Dashboard writes "thinking off, status marks silenced, status card off" at once, for chats that just want the conclusion. It is a one-time write; turning the preset off later does **not** revert the three switches, so turn each one back on yourself.

### Hiding card buttons

![Live card button switches](/img/streaming-card-button-settings.png)

Toggle each one under "Live card buttons" in the Dashboard, or:

```bash
/botconfig set hiddenStreamingCardButtons writeLink close
```

Values: `output` (show output, export text, refresh), `terminal`, `writeLink`, `compact` (including idle auto-compact), `stop`, `close`. `/botconfig unset hiddenStreamingCardButtons` shows them all again.

### Other card-related switches

| Setting | What it does | Default |
|---------|--------------|---------|
| `writableTerminalLinkInCard` | Puts a writable terminal button in the card; anyone who sees the card can operate the terminal, so only enable it in trusted chats | Off |
| `privateCard` | In regular groups, `/card` sends an admin-only static snapshot (it does not keep updating) | Off |
| `replyCardActions` | Shows an "Open terminal / Switch model / Close session" menu at the bottom right of ordinary reply cards | Off |

All of these can be changed in the Dashboard or with `/botconfig set <setting> on|off`.

## Pinning the current status card

With `pinStreamingCard` on, Botmux pins the **current public status card** to the top of the chat so the terminal and close buttons are always within reach.

* Per bot, off by default. Change it in the Dashboard or with `/botconfig set pinStreamingCard on|off`; existing sessions try to follow right away.
* Only the current public status card is pinned. Repo pickers, private `/card` snapshots, reply cards, the thinking process, close cards and so on are never pinned.
* Lark pins are per chat: with several topics or bots running in one chat, you may see several pins at once.
* To stop pinning in one chat: `/card pin off`; to restore: `/card pin on`; `/card pin status` tells you whether it's off at the bot level, off for this chat, or active.
* Pinning is best-effort: failures never affect posting, closing, relaying or anything else, and during errors you may briefly see no pin or an extra one. Botmux only removes pins it created itself, never pins from people or other apps.

## Reply card footer

![Reply card footer settings](/img/reply-footer-settings.png)

The footer at the bottom of the final reply card can show the items below; toggle each under "Reply card footer" in the Dashboard:

| Setting | Content | Default |
|---------|---------|---------|
| `replyFooterEnabled` | Master switch; when off the whole footer is hidden and the item settings are kept | On |
| `replyFooterBrand` | Brand signature (customize the text with `brandLabel`) | On |
| `replyFooterModel` | Model name, reasoning effort, backend spec | On |
| `replyFooterUsage` | Usage | On |
| `replyFooterRecipients` | Recipients and their @ notifications; when off the footer no longer @-mentions anyone, while explicit @ in the body is unaffected | On |
| `replyFooterVoice` | Voice summary button | On |
| `showReplyTiming` | Waiting and execution time | Off |

### Where usage is shown

The usage line looks like `ctx 23% · 5h 18% · 7d 5% · This turn ↑12k ↓3k · Total ↑1.2M ↓80k · Cache hit 92%`. Missing items are simply left out.

`usageDisplay` decides where it goes:

| Value | Location |
|-------|----------|
| `streaming` (default) | In the status card body, with full usage |
| `footer` | In the final reply footer, context and account quotas only |
| `off` | Not shown |

This only affects display, not usage accounting.

### Showing timing

Off by default. Turn it on in the Dashboard under **Bot Config → Message cards → Task Cards → Waiting and execution time**, or send `/botconfig set showReplyTiming on` (`showReplyTiming` in `bots.json`). Once on, the final reply footer shows "waited 3.2s · ran 23.4s", starting with newly received messages.

* **Waiting**: from Botmux accepting the message to actually handing it to the CLI, including queueing and cold start.
* **Execution**: from handing it to the CLI to seeing the final output. Codex App uses its own completion time.

Neither includes Lark delivery time. When timing can't be determined reliably (retries, restored old sessions, messages the model sent early via `botmux send`), it is not shown rather than guessed.

### Appending your own text to the usage line

Want gateway quotas, build status or who's on call after the usage line? Configure a command on the bot in bots.json:

```json
"cardFooterExtension": {
  "command": "~/.botmux/scripts/quota.sh",
  "refreshSeconds": 60
}
```

The command prints one segment per line, or JSON `{"segments": ["…", "…"]}`. For example, this output:

```
01 5h 2% 7d 2%
02 5h 4% 7d 2%
```

renders as `ctx 14% · 01 5h 2% 7d 2% · 02 5h 4% 7d 2%`.

Rules:

* At most 4 segments of at most 40 characters each, shown as plain text (Markdown is escaped).
* Run with `/bin/sh -c`, 3-second timeout, stdin closed, non-zero exit counts as failure. The environment includes `BOTMUX_LARK_APP_ID`, `BOTMUX_CLI_ID` and `BOTMUX_BOT_NAME` (the bot's configured CLI).
* No timer: a background refresh starts only while cards are rendered and the result is older than `refreshSeconds` (default 60, range 10–3600); rendering never waits for the command. All of a bot's sessions share one result.
* On failure the last good result is kept; once the last success is older than 10 minutes nothing is shown.
* Works for every CLI; follows `usageDisplay` and is hidden with it under `off`.

## Automatic-recovery failure card

When an ordinary Claude message hits a transient model failure (API unreachable, DNS outage, dropped stream, ...), Botmux continues it automatically, at most twice. If it still fails in the end, a failure card is posted in the original chat (or topic). It is the only notice for that message:

* It @-mentions the original sender, states the cause in one sentence (no raw error text), and adds an excerpt of the message, the time and how many continuations ran.
* **🔁 Retry** sends the message again as the original sender; the answer still goes to the original chat or topic. Only the original sender (while they can still talk to the bot) or a bot admin can press it. Each card can be retried successfully once, then shows who retried. The retried message asks the AI to check the current state first and avoid repeating work already done.
* A continuation that never produces a result (terminal idle for about a minute) also counts as failed, instead of staying "in progress" forever.
* If the Lark API is also down when the card is due, it keeps retrying (up to 24 hours) and lands exactly once; a daemon restart won't send it twice.
* Failed scheduled tasks get the card too, without a Retry button; run the task again manually if needed.

## Stop, retry and spend {#stop-retry-cost}

* **⏹ Stop**: there by default, shown on the status card only while the turn is still running. It is the same as pressing ^C and keeps the session; `/stop` in the topic does the same. Codex App sessions and sessions with `codexRpcInput` on can't be stopped this way; pressing it only suggests `/close`. To hide the button: `/botconfig set hiddenStreamingCardButtons stop`, or switch it off under the Dashboard's live card buttons (see [Hiding card buttons](#hiding-card-buttons) above).
* **🔁 Retry**: available on failure cards by default; the original sender or a bot admin can press it (see [Automatic-recovery failure card](#automatic-recovery-failure-card) above). For other failed or interrupted turns, send `/retry` in the topic.
* **Spend**: botmux only converts token usage into CNY after you set `pricing` for the bot in `bots.json` (the simplest is `"pricing": { "usdCny": 7.2 }`, which uses the built-in price table); without it the amount stays 0. In the current version the amount feeds monthly budget alerts (`budget`) and is not shown on cards; see [Spend and budget](/botmux/en/bots-json.md#budget). What the cards do show is the token usage line, see [Where usage is shown](#where-usage-is-shown) above.

## Richer messages with `botmux send`

Messages the agent sends with `botmux send` are separate messages that can carry images, files, videos and @ mentions. See [CLI commands](/botmux/en/cli-commands.md) for all flags. These are the ones most related to cards.

### Custom cards

`--card-file` / `--card-json` send raw Lark interactive card JSON.

> ⚠️ Custom cards allow **display-only content and open\_url buttons only**. Any callback control (buttons with a `value`, dropdowns, person pickers, date pickers, inputs, form submits) is rejected, so custom cards can't forge interactive callbacks.

### Videos, @mentions, urgent pings and dry runs {#send-rich}

These are all `botmux send` flags. The agent in the session calls them as needed; there is nothing to switch on:

| Want to | Flags |
|---|---|
| Send a video with a preview | `--videos <mp4>` plus `--video-covers <image>`, paired in order, both repeatable |
| Send a custom card | `--card-json '<json>'` or `--card-file <path>` (display-only content and open\_url buttons, see above) |
| @mention someone | `--mention <open_id>` (repeatable; with `allowArbitraryMention` on for the bot, a full email / phone / union\_id also works, as long as the person is in the group); `--mention-back` @mentions this turn's sender. Every reply must pick one of `--mention`, `--mention-back` or `--no-mention` |
| Send an urgent ping | `--urgent` (in-app, default), `--urgent=sms` or `--urgent=phone`, targeting this turn's sender; **must be used with `--mention-back`**. The app needs the matching `im:message.urgent*` permission; SMS / phone consume tenant quota |
| Check before sending | `--dry-run` renders the body as a card and prints JSON plus warnings without sending (no image / file uploads, no @ resolution) |

See `botmux send --help` for the full list.

### Semantic reply headers (`--layout`)

At key moments you can give a reply a colored header and tag:

```bash
botmux send --layout result --mention-back "Build passed and deployed to staging"
```

Choose `result`, `progress`, `risk` (needs confirmation), `blocked` or `handoff`. Without `--layout` it's an ordinary reply card. It does not apply to custom cards or voice messages.

In the Dashboard under "Bot config → Reply Style" you can set whether the five writing recipes are injected for the agent, whether `--layout` may add headers, the theme (default / minimal / vivid), and each header's color and tag. Running sessions pick up the new settings after a restart.

### Charts in messages (vega-lite)

A ` ```vega-lite ` block in the body renders as a native Lark chart:

````markdown
```vega-lite
{
  "mark": "bar",
  "data": {"values": [{"day": "Mon", "n": 3}, {"day": "Tue", "n": 5}]},
  "encoding": {
    "x": {"field": "day", "type": "nominal", "title": "Day"},
    "y": {"field": "n", "type": "quantitative", "title": "Count"}
  }
}
```
````

What's supported:

* Inline `data.values` only, at most 500 rows; values are string / number / boolean / null.
* `mark`: `bar` (horizontal when only x is quantitative), `line`, `area`, `point`, `arc` (pie; `innerRadius > 0` for a donut). A pie takes only `theta` (value) and `color` (category); no `x` / `y`, and `theta` has no `title`.
* Encoding channels: `x`, `y`, `color` (series), `theta`; each accepts only `field`, `type`, `title`. `x` / `y` titles become axis titles and the `color` title becomes the legend title.
* `type: temporal` is not parsed as a date; values show as categories in the given order, so sort them first.
* At most 5 charts per card. The whole message must fit Lark's 30 KB; when it doesn't, charts step down "chart → 50-row table → 10-row table → note only".

For safety, Botmux rebuilds charts from the fields it recognizes and rejects `data.url`, `transform`, `params`, `expr`, `signal`, `datasets`, `layer` and similar. Unsupported or oversized charts become a one-line note plus a plain data table, the reason is printed on stderr, and the message is still sent.

**Preview before sending**: `botmux send --dry-run` sends nothing and needs no session; it prints `{dryRun, bytes, fits, diagnostics, card}`, where `bytes` is the real Lark request size. It renders the body only: no image/file upload, no @ resolution, no footer.

### Updating a card in place after sending (card patch)

A successful `botmux send --card-file/--card-json` prints `{"success":true,"messageId":"om_...",...}`. With that messageId, `botmux card patch` **updates the same card in place** without sending a new message, which suits progress cards:

```bash
# 1. Send an "in progress" card and pull out the messageId with jq
MID=$(botmux send --card-file /tmp/progress.json --no-mention | jq -r .messageId)

# 2. Update it to 50%
botmux card patch --message-id "$MID" --card-json '{"schema":"2.0","header":{"template":"blue","title":{"tag":"plain_text","content":"Deploy progress"}},"body":{"direction":"vertical","elements":[{"tag":"markdown","content":"Progress: 50%"}]}}'

# 3. Update once more when done
botmux card patch --message-id "$MID" --card-json '{"schema":"2.0","header":{"template":"green","title":{"tag":"plain_text","content":"Deploy done"}},"body":{"direction":"vertical","elements":[{"tag":"markdown","content":"✅ Shipped"}]}}'
```

* The updated card goes through the same safety check as sending (display-only + open\_url).
* The `send` example passes `--no-mention`: every reply must pick one of `--mention` / `--mention-back` / `--no-mention`, or it is blocked (exit 2).
* The bot identity comes from the current session. Errors such as a withdrawn message, missing permission or a non-card target are reported as-is (exit 1); usage errors exit 2. On success stdout is a single line of JSON.

## Signed button: the clicker starts a turn as themselves (integrators)

A local integration can have the bot post a **single-use button card** into a chat. Whoever clicks the button starts the turn, just as if they had sent a message themselves. With `triggerUserAuth` on (`credentialSource: local`), credentials are issued for the clicker too, never falling back to the session owner.

### How to post one

Call the daemon's local IPC endpoint `POST /api/cards/click-turn` (same local HMAC auth as `/api/sessions/spawn`; not a public route). Request body:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `prompt` | Required. Becomes this turn's user input when clicked, at most 1500 characters |
| `chatId` / `sessionId` | Exactly one. A chat's chat-scope session, or an existing session |
| `postChatId` | Which chat to post the card in; defaults to `chatId`, required when only `sessionId` is given |
| `workingDir` | Optional existing absolute path. Required when the click would create a session |
| `chatType` | Optional, `group` or `p2p` |
| `ttlMs` | Optional, 1 minute to 7 days, default 1 hour |
| `buttonLabel` / `title` | Optional |

Success returns `{ ok, messageId, exp }`; if the bot is not in the target chat you get 403 `bot_not_in_chat`.

### Safety rules

* The daemon signs the button and **each button works once**; tampered, expired and repeated clicks are rejected, and a restart doesn't make it reusable.
* The clicker must both be allowed to talk to the bot and have operate rights (admin). People with talk-only grants can't use it; with `restrictGrantCommands` on, people whose talk access comes only from a per-user grant (chat guest `chatGrants` or global guest `globalGrants`) can't either; members of a fully opened group are not affected by this rule.
* A bot or app clicking does not start a turn and never falls back to the owner.
* A `sessionId` only matches an active session of this bot; a miss is rejected rather than spawning a new one. If the `chatId` has no session yet, one is created with the clicker as owner; an existing session whose working directory differs from the signed one is rejected.
* A new session without a signed `chatType` is treated as a group; private chats must be signed `p2p`.
* In sessions with cross-person interruption (`crossPrincipalInterruption`) or per-person lanes, clicks are rejected with a message explaining why.

After a click Lark first shows "starting"; once the CLI actually accepts the input, the chat gets "Started this turn as you". If delivery fails, the turn's changes are rolled back and a failure notice is posted instead.



---
url: /botmux/en/cli-commands.md
---

# CLI Commands

`botmux` commands come in two kinds:

* **Operator commands**: you run them in a server terminal to manage the daemon (the background process), bots, and sessions.
* **In-session commands**: the AI calls them inside a session to send messages, read history, create scheduled tasks, and so on. You usually don't type these yourself.

If you forget an option, run `botmux --help` for an overview, or `botmux <subcommand> --help` for the full options of one command.

## Most-used commands

| I want to… | Command |
|------|------|
| Configure for the first time / add a bot | `botmux setup` |
| Start / stop / restart | `botmux start` / `botmux stop` / `botmux restart` |
| Check whether it's running | `botmux status` |
| View logs | `botmux logs` |
| Upgrade | `botmux upgrade` |
| See active sessions, open a terminal | `botmux list` |
| Open the Dashboard | `botmux dashboard` |
| Start on boot | `botmux autostart enable` |

## Configure bots

### Interactive setup

```bash
botmux setup
```

Opens an interactive UI to configure for the first time, or add, edit, or delete bots. By default it signs in with a Lark QR scan and creates the app, grants permissions, sets the redirect, and publishes a version for you. Add `--no-open-platform-auto` to skip the automatic Open Platform setup.

### Scripted setup (no interactive UI)

Good for scripts or for letting an AI do it:

| Command | Purpose |
|------|------|
| `botmux setup list [--json]` | List configured bots (secrets masked) |
| `botmux setup add --create-app --allowed-users <owner>` | Scan a QR code to create a new Lark app and add it |
| `botmux setup add --app-id <cli_xxx> --app-secret <secret> --allowed-users <owner>` | Add a bot using an existing app's credentials |
| `botmux setup configure <process name\|AppID>` | Re-run Open Platform setup (permissions, events, publishing) for an added bot, e.g. when the last run didn't finish |
| `botmux setup edit <process name\|AppID> --cli codex` | Change individual fields, such as the CLI; pass `-` to clear a field |
| `botmux setup remove <process name\|AppID> --yes` | Delete a bot |

`--allowed-users` is the bot owner. When creating a new app, use a **full email, phone number, or a union\_id starting with `on_`**, not an open\_id starting with `ou_`: an open\_id is valid only in the Lark app that issued it, and the new app doesn't exist yet, so it can't have a valid open\_id. See `botmux setup help` for every field.

### Clone a bot

```bash
botmux clone <bot name> [--name <new name>]
```

Creates a new Lark app and copies the source bot's behavior settings. Without a name, it is named "source-name-copy-timestamp".

### Export a shareable preset

```bash
botmux preset export <bot> [--from-chat <chatId>] [--out <file>] [--yes]
```

Exports a bot's CLI, model, role, and capability tag as JSON, with setup guidance included. Send it to a teammate and their AI can set up a matching bot from it.

* `<bot>` is the process name (`botmux-xxx`) or AppID.
* The team-level role is exported by default; add `--from-chat <chatId>` to export the role content of one group instead (the group ID itself is not written to the file).
* By default it writes `<name>.botmux-preset.json` in the current directory; `--out -` prints to stdout.
* Before exporting, it shows you the role content to confirm. In non-interactive environments (for example when an AI runs it), add `--yes`.
* The file **contains no secrets**: AppID, Secret, `allowedUsers`, working directory, and similar fields are never exported.

### Switch the UI language

```bash
botmux lang          # Show the current language
botmux lang en       # Switch to English (zh / en)
botmux lang en --bot 0   # Change only bot #0 in bots.json
```

#### Switching languages in the setup wizard {#setup-lang}

While running `botmux setup`, press **L** on the first step's selection menu (with the search box empty) and the UI switches between Chinese and English right away; the choice is also saved as this machine's global language. In the simple numbered-input mode, typing `L` and Enter does the same.

You can also pick the language at launch: `botmux setup --lang en` (or `zh`), which is saved as the global language too. To change the UI language later, use `botmux lang` above.

## Start and stop the daemon

| Command | Description |
|------|------|
| `botmux start` | Start the daemon, plus plugin services with `mode=auto` |
| `botmux stop` | Stop the daemon. Plugin services keep running unless you add `--with-plugin` |
| `botmux restart` | Restart the daemon; active sessions are restored automatically |
| `botmux status` | Show the status of the daemon and each bot |
| `botmux logs` | View logs. Shows the last 50 lines and keeps following by default |
| `botmux start-bot <AppID>` | Start one bot only, without restarting the others. If the daemon as a whole isn't running, it tells you to use `botmux start` first |
| `botmux stop-bot <AppID>` | Stop one bot only; the other bots are unaffected |

`start-bot` / `stop-bot` accept `--json` for machine-readable output, handy in scripts. `botmux setup add` and Dashboard bot creation use `start-bot` to bring a new bot online.

Common `botmux logs` options:

* `--lines N`: show the last N lines.
* `--bot <index|name|AppID>`: show one bot only (index starts at 0).
* `--no-follow`: print and exit instead of following.

`start` / `restart` also accept `--companion-secret-file <absolute path> --companion-bot <appId>`. Passing both enables a closed local API for one isolated test bot; see [Local Companion API](/botmux/en/companion-api.md).

## Upgrade

```bash
botmux upgrade            # Upgrade to the latest stable release (alias: botmux update)
botmux upgrade canary     # Switch to a preview channel: canary / beta / rc / next
botmux upgrade 3.28.0     # Install a specific version
```

When it finishes, run `botmux restart` as prompted to load the new version. If you run botmux from a source checkout, `upgrade` does `git pull` + rebuild + restart instead. On releases older than v3.18.0, upgrade with the curl install script instead; see [FAQ · How do I upgrade?](/botmux/en/faq.md#how-do-i-upgrade).

## Manage sessions

### View sessions: `botmux list`

```bash
botmux list          # Interactive list (alias: ls)
botmux list --plain  # Plain-text table for scripts / pipes
botmux list --json   # JSON output
```

Keys in the interactive list:

| Key | Action |
|------|------|
| `↑` / `↓` (or `k` / `j`) | Select a session |
| `Enter` | Attach to the managed tmux / ZMX terminal; a suspended session is resumed first |
| `d` (or `x`) | Delete the selected session (press `y` to confirm) |
| `q` / `Esc` | Quit |

`list` also cleans up dead sessions: adopt sessions whose external process has exited, and throwaway sessions that never actually launched a CLI. A regular session is kept even if its CLI process exits; the next message picks it up again.

### Close, resume, suspend

| Command | Description |
|------|------|
| `botmux delete <id>` | Close a session (aliases `del` / `rm`). The first few characters of the ID are enough; if several match, you'll be asked for a longer prefix |
| `botmux delete all` | Close all active sessions |
| `botmux delete stopped` | Clean up zombie sessions whose process has exited (suspended sessions that can still resume are left alone) |
| `botmux resume <id>` | Resume a closed session and relaunch the CLI with its previous context (local sessions relaunch when the next message arrives) |
| `botmux suspend <id\|all>` | Suspend a session: the CLI process ends, but the session stays, and the next message picks up the context |
| `botmux suspend --bot <appId>` | Suspend all sessions of one bot |
| `botmux suspend --isolated` | Suspend sessions of every bot with read isolation. Use after updating CLI login credentials; the next launch syncs the new credentials |

Every `suspend` form accepts `--dry-run` to preview which sessions would be affected.

`delete` has the same effect as sending `/close` in Lark. When the daemon is online, it does the cleanup; if the daemon refuses or can't be reached, the command fails instead of killing processes locally. Local cleanup happens only once the daemon is confirmed offline.

### Suspend long-idle sessions in bulk

```bash
botmux maintenance suspend-idle --older-than 7d --dry-run   # Preview first
botmux maintenance suspend-idle --older-than 7d --yes       # Then execute
```

* `--older-than` is the last-activity threshold, in `ms/s/m/h/d/w`; default `7d`.
* `--dry-run` only lists candidates (session, bot, title, last activity, processes to be stopped) and changes nothing. Running for real requires an explicit `--yes`.
* `--bot <appId>` limits it to one bot; `--json` gives machine-readable output.
* Suspended sessions are kept; the next message cold-starts them from history.
* Only sessions that are clearly idle and resumable are picked. Sessions that are replying, have queued messages, are waiting on you, are locked, or were attached via adopt are skipped.

To run this periodically, turn on "Idle auto-suspend" in the bot settings in the Dashboard. This command is for manual previews and one-off batches.

### Get an operable terminal link

```bash
botmux term-link [id]
```

Gets a writable Web terminal for a session. The link isn't printed in the terminal; the daemon sends it to the bot owner as a private card (only you can see it in a group; in topics or direct chats it falls back to a direct message). You can omit `id` when there's only one active session. See [Web Terminal](/botmux/en/web-terminal.md).

## Dashboard login link

```bash
botmux dashboard           # Get the current login URL (same as dashboard current; creates one if missing)
botmux dashboard rotate    # Issue a new token; the old link stops working
```

See [Dashboard](/botmux/en/dashboard.md) for what it can do.

## Start on boot

```bash
botmux autostart enable   # Register start-on-boot (no sudo needed)
botmux autostart disable  # Unregister
botmux autostart status   # Show status
```

| OS | How it's done |
|------|------|
| macOS | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.botmux.daemon.plist` (launchd) |
| Linux | `~/.config/systemd/user/botmux.service` (user systemd), plus the crash watchdog `botmux-watchdog.timer` |
| Windows | A per-user scheduled task; falls back to the Startup folder if registering the task is denied |

Keep in mind:

* **On Linux servers, logging out stops the service.** To keep it running, run `sudo loginctl enable-linger <username>` once.
* The entry records the current Node (or single-file binary) path. After switching Node versions with nvm / fnm, run `enable` again; `start` / `restart` also detect and refresh it automatically.
* `enable` / `disable` **only manage start-on-boot; they never start or stop the running daemon**.
* On Linux, `enable` also turns on `botmux-watchdog.timer`: it checks every 30 seconds and brings the daemon back if it dies unexpectedly; `disable` turns it off too. After you run `botmux stop` on purpose, the watchdog won't bring it back; normal watching resumes on the next `start` / `restart`. `botmux autostart status` shows whether the watchdog is enabled.

## In-session commands (for the AI)

When run inside a botmux session, these commands detect the current session and group automatically, so no extra options are needed. The AI calls them as needed; it's enough for you to know what's available.

### Messages and cards

| Command | Description |
|------|------|
| `botmux send [content]` | Send a message to the current topic. Content can come from stdin / heredoc / `--content-file`. Common options: `--images`, `--files`, `--videos` (with `--video-covers`), `--card-file` / `--card-json` (custom card), `--mention` / `--mention-back` / `--no-mention` (who to @), `--diff` (collapsible code-change preview), `--voice` (voice bubble), `--dry-run` (render without sending). See `botmux send --help` for all options |
| `botmux card patch --message-id <om_xxx> (--card-file <path> \| --card-json <json>)` | Update a custom card previously sent by `send`, in place, without a new message. The messageId comes from the `send` output |
| `botmux card stream open/write/finish ...` | Stream text into a custom card with a typewriter effect, and optionally bind the daemon's runtime status to the card. See `botmux card stream --help` for the full flow |
| `botmux ask buttons --options "a,b" "<question>"` | Send a multiple-choice question as a button card and return the user's choice. `--multi` allows several choices |
| `botmux ask buttons --questions-file <file>` | Put several questions (choice, text, number, with presets) in one card, submitted once; returns all answers |
| `botmux ask buttons --answerer <open_id> ...` | Only the given person can submit (this limits who answers; it is not a business approval) |
| `botmux history [--limit N]` | Read the current session's message history (JSON). In a topic it reads the topic; in a regular group, the whole group |
| `botmux history --scope ambient` | In a topic session, read the group context outside the topic. `--scope` takes `session` / `thread` / `chat` / `ambient` |
| `botmux history --with-card-json` | Attach the raw structured JSON of each card |
| `botmux quoted <message_id>` | Read the single quoted message; attachments are downloaded locally |
| `botmux bots list` | List the bots in the current group (with open\_id, for `--mention`) |
| `botmux bots list --scope team` | Discover opted-in bots from the same team on other machines (by expertise), to create or fill a group |
| `botmux bots invite --chat <chatId> --team <id> --agent <appId>...` | Add same-team bots, together with their owners, to an existing group; see `botmux bots invite --help` |

### Sessions and groups

| Command | Description |
|------|------|
| `botmux session rename "<title>"` | Rename the **current session**. Dashboard and the `/sessions` list update immediately. The Lark group name and topic name don't change. Suggested shape: "type | subject", up to 200 characters |
| `botmux chat rename <new name> [--proactive]` | Rename the **Lark group** hosting the current session (in a topic group this renames the whole group, visible to all members). `--proactive` marks an AI-initiated rename, limited to once per 10 minutes |
| `botmux top-notice set <message_id>` | Pin one message in the current group as the group top notice. Works only in group sessions, or pass `--chat-id` to pick the group |
| `botmux slash "/command"` | Once the CLI is idle, inject one native slash command (such as `/compact`) into this session's CLI; see the notes below |
| `botmux preview <port>` | Register a local web service started in the session, so you can preview it after signing in to the Dashboard without exposing the local address |
| `botmux role switch <role dir>` | Switch the current topic to a role (the directory must be under `~/botmux-roles`); see [Roles](/botmux/en/roles.md) |
| `botmux skill list` / `skill show <name>` | List / read available skill instructions |

`botmux slash` **rejects everything by default**. First set `tuiSlashAllow` for the bot in [bots.json](/botmux/en/bots-json.md), listing the command names allowed, for example `["/compact"]` (case-insensitive; the leading `/` is optional). Also:

* Only single-line commands starting with `/` are accepted; arguments may follow, and the command name is matched against the list.
* `/cd` is always rejected, even if listed: it changes the session directory the daemon tracks, so it must go through a dedicated command.
* The command is queued until the CLI is idle; if the CLI process restarts before then, the command is dropped.

### Lark authorization

| Command | Description |
|------|------|
| `botmux auth request [--scope "<scope1 scope2>"] [--json]` | Generate a Lark authorization link for the person who sent this turn, returned as JSON. The AI sends the link to the user to click |
| `botmux auth wait --request-id <id> [--json]` | Wait for that authorization to finish, up to 5 minutes. On success, retry the original action |

#### Agent-initiated authorization {#agent-auth-request}

**Nothing to set up on the user's side.** When the AI calls a Lark API with `lark-cli --as user` in a session and finds your authorization missing, it runs `botmux auth request` itself (asking for all the scopes it needs in one `--scope`) and sends the link to **the person who sent this turn**:

* in a direct chat, the AI replies with the link;
* in a group, botmux sends the link to you in a private message, never into the group.

After you authorize, the AI waits for it with `botmux auth wait` in the same turn (up to 5 minutes) and retries the original action. If the turn has already ended, that's fine: authorize while the link is valid, then send another message to continue. You can also skip the wait and send `/login` (or `/login --scope <scope>`) in the topic yourself.

Prerequisite: this bot's `lark-cli` goes through botmux's app binding (`larkToolBinding`, on by default), or the bot has [Run CLI calls as the message sender](/botmux/en/bots-json.md#trigger-user-auth) on with `lark-cli` covered. With both off, the daemon refuses with `lark_user_auth_disabled`. The link only goes to the verified human of the current turn; the AI cannot request it on someone else's behalf.

### Read-only queries

These commands only read state; they change nothing.

| Command | Description |
|------|------|
| `botmux observe [--session <id>] [--lark-app <appId>]` | Query session and worker state live through the daemon (JSON). If it can't get an answer it shows unknown and never reads a cache |
| `botmux execution current --json` | Check which bot, session, turn, and worker the current process belongs to |
| `botmux actor current --json` | Return the daemon-verified enterprise email of this turn's sender, plus the current group ID and turn ID (no open\_id). Refused when not run inside a session process |

### Advanced features (each has its own page)

| Command | Purpose | See |
|------|------|------|
| `botmux schedule add/list/update/remove/pause/resume/run/done` | Scheduled tasks | [Scheduled Tasks](/botmux/en/schedule.md) |
| `botmux dispatch` / `botmux report` | Open sub-topics, hand tasks to other bots, and report results back | [Multi-topic](/botmux/en/multi-topic.md) |
| `botmux project ...` | Maintain a pinned project progress card in a regular group | [Project Progress Card](/botmux/en/project-card.md) |
| `botmux workflow ...` | Multi-step orchestrated workflows | [Workflow](/botmux/en/workflow.md) |
| `botmux goal run <goal>` | Run one goal headless from the command line; `--json` prints the result | [Workflow](/botmux/en/workflow.md) |
| `botmux create-group --bot <name> [--bot ...]` | Create a Lark group with one or more bots | [Multi-bot](/botmux/en/multi-bot.md) |
| `botmux board ...` | Decision board (steward bot sessions only) | [Decision Board](/botmux/en/decision-board.md) |
| `botmux whiteboard ...` | Local project whiteboard | [Whiteboard](/botmux/en/whiteboard.md) |

For how the AI discovers and uses these commands, see [Skill + CLI](/botmux/en/skill-cli.md).

### Create a group that starts working, or a topic group {#create-group}

`botmux create-group` runs from a host terminal or inside a session; there is no switch to turn on:

```bash
botmux create-group --bot reviewer-a --bot reviewer-b --name "PR #123 review" \
  --chat-mode topic \
  --kickoff-bot ou_xxx --kickoff-prompt "Please review PR #123"
```

* `--bot`: at least one, repeatable. Prefer the bot's display name or full AppID. **The first one is the creator.**
* `--chat-mode topic`: create a topic group (each top-level message is its own topic); `group` or leaving it out makes a regular group. The group type can only be chosen at creation and cannot be changed later.
* `--kickoff-bot` + `--kickoff-prompt`: once the group exists, the creator @mentions that bot with this prompt so it starts working right away (for example, a PR review). Give both together. `--kickoff-bot` is that bot's open\_id (look it up with `botmux bots list` in a session); it must be in the `--bot` list and cannot be the first one.
* `--working-dir <path>`: binds the new group to this directory for every bot that joined, so new topics skip the repo picker.
* `--json-status`: prints a structured status line after the chatId. With or without it, the command exits non-zero when a requested kickoff wasn't sent.

See `botmux create-group --help` for every flag, including cross-machine team groups (`--team` / `--agent`).

## Other configuration commands

| Command | Purpose | See |
|------|------|------|
| `botmux voice` | Configure voice summaries and speech recognition | [Voice](/botmux/en/voice.md) |
| `botmux plugin ...` | Create, install, and enable plugins | [Plugins](/botmux/en/plugins.md) |
| `botmux sandbox-network-policy ...` | Configure network access policy for local Linux sessions | [Sandbox](/botmux/en/sandbox.md) |
| `botmux env-policy get\|set\|unset` | Configure which environment variables bot processes inherit | [bots.json](/botmux/en/bots-json.md) |
| `botmux worker-budget status\|set\|unset` | View or adjust the memory check run before a session starts | [Global Settings](/botmux/en/global-settings.md) |
| `botmux feedback storage ...` | View or switch where feedback data is stored (SQLite / PostgreSQL) | [Feedback Storage & Migration](/botmux/en/feedback-storage.md) |
| `botmux session start/send/publish ...` / `botmux headless ...` | Start sessions and fetch results from scripts or CI without a Lark group | [Headless Automation Sessions](/botmux/en/headless-session.md) |
| `botmux model-proxy serve` | Start a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint (experimental) | [Model Proxy](/botmux/en/model-proxy.md) |

## Advanced: multi-replica deployments (primary mode)

Single-machine deployments can skip this section.

With `BOTMUX_COORDINATION_MODE=primary`, session state lives in PostgreSQL and is shared across machines (replicas). In this mode:

* Local `delete`, `resume`, `suspend` (except `--dry-run`), `maintenance suspend-idle`, and delete / resume inside `list` are refused. Close or resume from the session card in the original topic, so the action goes through the shared session-control channel.
* `list` still works, but only displays sessions and never cleans up local ones.

A session runs only on the replica that owns it, while Lark callbacks and browser requests may land on any replica:

* **"Show / Hide output" button**: applied by the owning replica, which updates the original card. It takes effect only for people allowed to operate the session; clicking an old card or lacking permission shows a hint to use the latest card.
* **Web terminal across replicas**: a request that lands on another replica is forwarded one hop to the owner. Configure:
  * `BOTMUX_TERMINAL_ROUTE_HOST`: the IP other replicas can reach this one at (e.g. the Pod IP); must be an IP. If unset, this replica doesn't take part in forwarding.
  * `BOTMUX_TERMINAL_ROUTE_PORT`: the port other replicas use for this Dashboard (e.g. a NodePort); defaults to `BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_PORT`.
  * Cookies, Authorization, and other login credentials are never forwarded.
* **What works across replicas**: only terminal links in Lark cards, which carry their own credential. The terminal embedded in the Dashboard, the touch-screen dynamic link, and takeover with write access must reach the owning replica directly (e.g. session-sticky load balancing); otherwise they return 403.
* Deployments without primary mode are unaffected.

url: /botmux/en/companion-api.md
---

# Local Companion API

The Companion API is a small, **local-only** interface. It lets your own tools on the same machine (test scripts, a desktop companion app, and so on) read and change two things on **one** test Bot:

* **Role**: the Bot's default role (persona) and how it is injected;
* **Runtime**: which CLI it uses (Codex or TRAE), which model, and which reasoning level.

It is off by default. When on, it is bound to the single Bot you name at startup. It does not reuse Dashboard login tokens and cannot proxy any other Dashboard route.

## Who it's for

| What you want to do | Good fit? |
|---|---|
| Script persona/model switches on a test Bot for comparison runs | Yes |
| Build a local companion app that tweaks a test Bot | Yes |
| Manage production Bots, several Bots, or call it from a remote service | No. Use the [Dashboard](/botmux/en/dashboard.md) or the [Task Trigger API](/botmux/en/api-task-trigger.md) |

## Step 1: Prepare a dedicated test Bot

In `bots.json`, set up a Bot that is **separate from your production Bots** and meets all three rules:

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| `larkAppId` | Appears only once in `bots.json` |
| `sandbox` | Set to `true` (turns on the [allowlist sandbox](/botmux/en/sandbox.md)). It must be the boolean `true`; the strings `"oncall"` / `"scratch"`, or `readIsolation` alone, are rejected |
| `cliId` | `codex` or `traex` (`codex-app` is not accepted) |

```json
{
  "larkAppId": "cli_xxx_test",
  "larkAppSecret": "…",
  "cliId": "codex",
  "sandbox": true
}
```

## Step 2: Prepare the secret file

The secret is a random string you generate yourself; it is used to sign requests. The file must:

* live at an **absolute path** that does not go through any symlink;
* be a regular file, not a symlink;
* be owned by the current user with mode `0600`;
* be non-empty and at most 1 KiB (leading/trailing whitespace is trimmed);
* sit in a directory that is also owned by the current user and not writable by group or others (so not a shared directory like `/tmp`).

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.secrets && chmod 700 ~/.secrets
openssl rand -base64 32 > ~/.secrets/botmux-companion
chmod 600 ~/.secrets/botmux-companion
```

## Step 3: Start

```bash
botmux restart \
  --companion-secret-file "$HOME/.secrets/botmux-companion" \
  --companion-bot cli_xxx_test
```

* Both `start` and `restart` accept these options, and they **must be given together**.
* You can use environment variables instead: `BOTMUX_COMPANION_SECRET_FILE` and `BOTMUX_COMPANION_BOT_APP_ID`.
* If the fleet is already running, `start` errors out; use `restart` to apply the options.
* If validation fails, startup is refused. Errors are fixed strings and never include the app id, file path, or secret:

| Error | Cause |
|---|---|
| `companion configuration requires both secret-file and bot selection` | Only one of the two options was given |
| `companion_secret_invalid` | The secret file doesn't meet Step 2 |
| `companion bot selection must match exactly one isolated codex/traex Bot` | The Bot is missing, duplicated, or doesn't meet Step 1 |

## Step 4: Send requests

The API lives on the Dashboard's local port (default `7891`; the actual port is written to `~/.botmux/.dashboard-port`). All paths start with `/__companion/v1/`.

### Signing

Every request carries three headers:

| Header | Content |
|---|---|
| `X-Botmux-Companion-Timestamp` | Current time in epoch milliseconds, within 60 seconds of the server clock |
| `X-Botmux-Companion-Nonce` | A fresh random value for every request; each can be used only once |
| `X-Botmux-Companion-Signature` | HMAC-SHA256 of the material below using the secret, base64url-encoded |

The signed material is five lines joined with `\n`:

```text
timestamp
nonce
METHOD (uppercase, e.g. GET / PUT)
path (e.g. /__companion/v1/role, no query string)
sha256 of the request body (hex; with no body, the sha256 of the empty string)
```

A ready-to-use Node.js example:

```js
import { createHash, createHmac, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';

const secret = readFileSync(`${process.env.HOME}/.secrets/botmux-companion`, 'utf8').trim();
const port = readFileSync(`${process.env.HOME}/.botmux/.dashboard-port`, 'utf8').trim();

async function call(method, path, body) {
  const raw = body === undefined ? '' : JSON.stringify(body);
  const timestamp = String(Date.now());
  const nonce = randomUUID();
  const bodyHash = createHash('sha256').update(raw).digest('hex');
  const signature = createHmac('sha256', secret)
    .update([timestamp, nonce, method, path, bodyHash].join('\n'))
    .digest('base64url');
  const res = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}${path}`, {
    method,
    headers: {
      'content-type': 'application/json',
      'X-Botmux-Companion-Timestamp': timestamp,
      'X-Botmux-Companion-Nonce': nonce,
      'X-Botmux-Companion-Signature': signature,
    },
    body: raw || undefined,
  });
  return res.json();
}

console.log(await call('GET', '/__companion/v1/health'));
```

### Routes

| Route | Purpose | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /__companion/v1/health` | Protocol version and capabilities | none |
| `GET /__companion/v1/role` | Read the default role | none |
| `PUT /__companion/v1/role` | Write the default role | `{requestId, role, injectMode}` |
| `GET /__companion/v1/runtime` | Read the runtime config | none |
| `PUT /__companion/v1/runtime` | Change the runtime config | `{requestId, provider, model?, reasoning?}` |

Success responses look like `{"ok": true, ...}`. `health` returns the protocol version `botmux.companion.v1` and a capability list; read routes put the result in `value`; write routes return the `requestId` plus the read-back `value` after the write.

**Reading and writing the role**

* A read returns `{role, injectMode, revision: null}`. This role is the "default role" from [Roles & Teams](/botmux/en/roles.md), the same one written by `/role team set` and the Dashboard's default-role editor.
* `role`: Markdown text, up to 32 KiB (UTF-8 bytes); an empty string `""` clears it.
* `injectMode`: `every` (inject every turn) or `once` (first turn only).

```js
await call('PUT', '/__companion/v1/role', {
  requestId: 'role-20261105-001',
  role: 'You are a strict code reviewer.',
  injectMode: 'every',
});
```

**Reading and writing the runtime**

* A read returns `{provider, model?, reasoning?}`; unset fields are omitted.
* `provider`: `codex` or `traecli`, mapped to Botmux `codex` and `traex`. Sending the other value switches the Bot to the other CLI.
* `model`: optional, at most 200 characters; omitting it clears any configured model and falls back to the CLI default.
* `reasoning`: optional reasoning level; only levels supported by that CLI and model are accepted (e.g. `low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh`); omitting it clears any configured level.
* Each write replaces the whole runtime config: to keep the current model or reasoning level, read first and send them back together.

```js
await call('PUT', '/__companion/v1/runtime', {
  requestId: 'runtime-20261105-001',
  provider: 'codex',
  model: '<model-name>',
  reasoning: 'high',
});
```

Bodies accept only the fields listed above; any extra field is rejected.

### Retries and requestId

* You generate `requestId`: 8–128 characters, letters, digits, `_` and `-` only.
* A **successful** write is remembered by `requestId` for 10 minutes; resending it does not run the operation again and returns the earlier result.
* Failed or timed-out results are not remembered, so you can retry with the same `requestId`.
* An operation that takes longer than 10 seconds returns `timeout`. The underlying change may still be in progress, so read the current value first before deciding to retry.

### Error codes

| HTTP status | `error` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_body` | Body is not valid JSON, has extra fields, has invalid values, or lacks `requestId` |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | Missing headers, timestamp outside 60 seconds, or bad signature |
| 403 | `forbidden` | The request did not come from loopback |
| 404 | `unknown_endpoint` | Path or method not in the table above (a query string counts too) |
| 404 | `companion_disabled` | The Companion API was not enabled for this run, or the Dashboard's own Bot/secret check failed at startup (look for `[companion] disabled` in the Dashboard log) |
| 409 | `replayed` | The nonce was already used |
| 413 | `body_too_large` | Body exceeds 64 KiB |
| 500 | `timeout` / `operation_failed` | The operation timed out or failed (for example, the bound Bot no longer meets Step 1); transient failures can be retried |

## Security boundaries

* **Local only**: requests must come from a loopback address such as `127.0.0.1`. If you explicitly enable the platform tunnel, requests arriving through it still have to pass signature checks; the signature is the real gate on that path.
* **Separate auth**: signatures are checked before, and independently of, normal Dashboard auth. Passing them grants no Dashboard admin identity.
* **Fixed scope**: no Bot ID, chat ID, arbitrary settings, env vars, URLs, headers, or commands are accepted. Every operation targets only the Bot bound at startup, and each one re-checks that the Bot still meets Step 1.
* **No leaks**: role text is returned only through this signed API and never appears in Dashboard/public data; responses and errors never contain the secret, file paths, or internal IDs.
