url: /botmux/en/dashboard.md
---

# Dashboard Control Panel

<video src="../img/video-v7-dashboard-en.mp4" controls preload="metadata" style="width:100%;border-radius:8px"></video>

The Dashboard is botmux's built-in web admin console. One page lets you manage sessions, groups, scheduled tasks, workflows, and configuration for **every bot** on this machine, without typing commands into each Lark group.

## Open the Dashboard

On the machine running botmux:

```bash
botmux dashboard          # Print the login link (creates a token on first run)
botmux dashboard rotate   # Switch to a new token; old links stop working immediately
```

`botmux dashboard current` does exactly the same as the bare command; it is just the explicit form.

The **first line of output is always the link and nothing else**, so scripts can use `botmux dashboard | head -1`. The following lines are:

* `工作台: …`: a link straight to the **Cockpit**, handy as a bookmark.
* A safety notice (see below).

The default port is `7891`; change it with the `BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_PORT` environment variable.

If you use the [macOS Desktop App](/botmux/en/desktop.md), you can open the Dashboard right from the App window.

### What the token in the link is

The token is a login credential, like a long-lived key:

* The same link logs you in again and again, and keeps working after `botmux restart`.
* Only `botmux dashboard rotate` changes the key, and the old link stops working.
* After you first open a `?t=<token>` link, the browser remembers the login and the token is removed from the address bar.

### When the link has no token

| How you deploy | What the link looks like | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Bound to the central platform (remote access on and bound) | `https://m-<machineId>.<platform-domain>/`, **no token** | The platform sends you through single sign-on first and knows who you are. The token does nothing here and would only be a leak risk |
| Your own reverse proxy (`BOTMUX_PUBLIC_URL`) or a Devbox short link | `https://<your-domain>/?t=<token>`, **with token** | The proxy only forwards requests and does not identify you, so the token is the only ticket in |
| LAN only | `http://<lan-ip>:7891/?t=<token>`, **with token** | Same as above |

The Dashboard itself decides whether to drop the token (it knows which address the link uses). When it cannot tell, it keeps the token: an extra token is a minor nuisance, a missing one can lock you out.

Once bound to the platform, the "local IP + token" direct link is hidden by default; it is only a fallback for when the platform has problems. If you really need it, rerun the command with the flag named in its output. That flag is deliberately left out of `--help` so an AI running automation does not add it by habit and write the token into a chat transcript.

:::warning The link is an admin password
Send a `?t=` link only to yourself. **Never paste it into a group chat**: chat history is kept for a long time and can be forwarded or screenshotted. When someone asks how to get in, tell them to run `botmux dashboard` on the server themselves.

If you suspect a leak, run `botmux dashboard rotate` right away; every old link stops working on the spot.
:::

### Browsing without logging in: read-only mode

Opening the Dashboard without a token puts you in **read-only mode** by default: you can see "watch the work" pages such as sessions, scheduled tasks, and the group list, but you cannot change anything, and admin pages like Bot Config, Skills, Webhook, and Terminal are hidden.

If you do not want people on your network to see this, turn off **Allow tokenless read-only dashboard access** under **Global Settings → General → Access**. The exact boundary is described in [Public read-only and the token boundary](#public-read-only-and-the-token-boundary).

## Pages at a glance

The left navigation has five groups. Pages marked 🔒 only appear after you log in with the token.

| Group | Page | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| Overview | Workbench | Home: online bots, items waiting for you, sessions at work |
| Collaboration | Session Control | View and manage every session (Kanban / Table views); details below |
| | Decision board | Make decisions in one place on the web; see [Decision Board & Steward](/botmux/en/decision-board.md). Appears only once at least one bot is a steward |
| | Cockpit | Work with several sessions side by side, chat with them and watch their terminals; see [Agent Workbench](/botmux/en/workbench.md) |
| | Group Management | Create groups, add bots, tune per-group settings and member access; details below |
| | Scheduled Tasks | Create, edit, pause, and run scheduled tasks now; see [Scheduled Tasks](/botmux/en/schedule.md) |
| | Workflows | Watch workflow runs and cancel them; see [Workflow](/botmux/en/workflow.md) |
| Digital Workforce | Role Management 🔒 | Give each bot a per-group persona; see [Roles & Team](/botmux/en/roles.md) |
| | Skill Management 🔒 | Install skills from a GitHub / Git address or a local directory |
| | Customization 🔒 | Override built-in prompts and skills, with export / import and rollback |
| | Message Listener 🔒 | Let bots respond to group messages by rule without an @, configurable per group |
| | Doc watches 🔒 | Manage Lark doc-comment watches; see [Doc Comments](/botmux/en/doc-comment.md) |
| | Bot Config 🔒 | Each bot's default behavior; details below |
| | Agents 🔒 | Reusable execution profiles (CLI, model, directory, sandbox) that several bots can share |
| Analytics | Monitoring Board | Machine health, memory, and session pressure |
| | Data Insights 🔒 | Statistics on sessions and tool calls; details below |
| | Feedback 🔒 | Rating coverage, latest ratings, and failures for final answers; to switch storage (SQLite / PostgreSQL), see [Feedback Storage & Migration](/botmux/en/feedback-storage.md) |
| Management | Terminal 🔒 | Web terminal for the local shell / tmux / herdr, shown only to the local owner |
| | Webhook 🔒 | Connectors and invocation logs; see [Connectors](/botmux/en/webhook.md) |
| | Plugins 🔒 | Manage plugins; see [Plugins](/botmux/en/plugins.md) |
| | Whiteboards 🔒 | Local whiteboards; see [Whiteboard](/botmux/en/whiteboard.md) |
| | Global Settings | Global switches for access, Lark cards, scheduled tasks, auto-update, auto-start, and more; see [Global Settings](/botmux/en/global-settings.md) |

The top of the sidebar also has **Create session** and **Create bot** shortcut buttons.

## Global search (⌘K)

Want to jump to a session or a setting quickly → press `⌘K` (macOS) or `Ctrl+K` (other systems) on any page, or click the search box in the top bar.

![⌘K global search](/img/dashboard-command-palette.png)

What you can find:

* **Sessions**, including closed ones.
* **Settings**: individual options in Global Settings and Bot Config (for example the session mode for standard groups). Picking one jumps there and highlights the row. If the current bot does not have that option, it stops at the category and tells you why.
* **Bots**: by name or app id, straight to that bot's config.
* **Skills / Agents**.
* **Pages**, including sub-pages not in the sidebar such as the Session Monitor Room, Webhook invocation logs, role Profiles, and each Data Insights tab.
* **Quick actions**, such as switching the theme.

Both Chinese and English names work. Skills, agents, and bots only show up for logged-in administrators.

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `↑` `↓` | Move the selection |
| `↵` | Open |
| `⌘↵` / `Ctrl+↵` | Secondary action: when logged in, open an active session in the Cockpit; otherwise jump to its Lark thread |
| `Tab` | Switch category |
| `Esc` | Close |

With an empty query, the list shows recently used items.

## Session Control

This page lists the sessions of every bot, in two views you switch at the top:

* **Kanban**: columns for Backlog / Todo / In Progress / Needs You / Done. Sessions land in a column automatically by status (for example a session waiting for you to pick a repo or confirm something goes to Needs You), and you can drag them to another column. Nothing lands in Backlog automatically: drag a session there, or pick Backlog when you **Create session** (the group and bots are set up, but the CLI does not start yet). Dormant sessions stay off the board by default; see them in the Table view.
* **Table**: good for bulk actions, with columns you can choose.

Both views filter by status, bot, chat, CLI, and source (Feishu-native / External `/adopt`), and you can search by chat name, working directory, title, or ID.

Common actions:

| What you want | How |
|---|---|
| Go back to the Lark thread | Click **Locate Topic**: the bot posts a message in the original thread that only @-mentions the session owner; tap the notification to jump back |
| Open the chat | Click **Open chat** |
| Look at the terminal | **Open read-only terminal** to watch; **Take over terminal** to type |
| The CLI is stuck | **Restart CLI**. If the session still has unfinished work, the restart is refused for now so nothing is lost |
| Close sessions | **Close Session**, or multi-select and **Close selected** |
| Bring back a closed session | **Resume Session** |
| Clean up idle sessions in bulk | **Clean idle**, choosing idle for more than 24 hours, 72 hours, or 7 days. Sessions waiting for you and locked sessions are left alone |
| Keep a session safe from Clean idle | **Lock session** |
| Watch several sessions at once | Multi-select and **Add to monitor room** to see several terminals on one screen in the Session Monitor Room |
| See what a session did | **Insight**: counts tool calls, failures, and time spent, with suggestions |
| Reproduce how the CLI was launched | **Copy reproduce command**. It contains credentials such as tokens, so keep it private |

### Run status, task status and TODOs {#session-status-todo}

Automatic, nothing to configure. Session cards show status in two layers:

* **Run status**: whether the CLI is idle or working right now (working, starting, analyzing, and so on).
* **Task status**: whether the work is finished. When a Claude Code / Codex session record still has open TODOs, the card carries a "TODO done/total" badge. Hover to preview the list, click to pin it so you can select and copy.

So a session whose CLI is already idle but still has unfinished TODOs lands in the board's **Todo** column instead of blending in with idle ones. CLIs whose TODOs can't be read are unaffected and are placed by run status. TODO contents are hidden in read-only mode without a login.

## Group Management

![Group Management: standard group list](/img/dashboard-groups-list.png)

At the top you switch between two kinds of chats:

* **Groups**: groups you created or added bots to. Each row shows which bots are in it, with **Add Bots**, **Duplicate**, and **Manage** on the right.
* **Session chats**: groups a bot created automatically from a private chat, one per session, sortable by Recently active or Created.

Common actions:

* **New Chat**: pick the bots to add, and optionally bind a working directory (new threads start right there instead of asking you to pick a repo). After creating the group botmux adds you and tries to transfer group ownership to you.
* **Duplicate**: create another group with the same bots, bound directory, and chat roles in one click.
* **Manage**: opens the group settings drawer with six tabs:

| Tab | Contents |
|---|---|
| Overview | Every bot's settings in this group at a glance: chat role, reply mode, Oncall dir, default model, serial input, idle close, run card, pin card. Click a row to open that bot's settings |
| Bot settings | Per bot for this group: reply mode, Oncall, default model for new threads, serial handling of multi-person messages, idle auto-close, run cards, pinning the live card |
| Collaboration | Standard group (bots respond independently) or Project group (one coordinator bot orchestrates, each subtask gets its own thread) |
| Member access | Managed from one bot's point of view: multi-select members for a **batch grant** (up to 50 at a time, optional message quota and duration, membership re-checked before writing), a **whole-chat grant** (same as sending a bare `/grant` in the group), and **Block / Unblock** for a single member |
| Recall messages | Pick one of the bots in the chat and page through the group's messages (or open a topic to read replies). You can only select messages sent by that bot **itself**, up to 50 per batch, with a success or failure result for each message. Lark's recall time limit applies |
| Leave / Disband | Have selected bots leave, or disband the group (only works when a bot is the owner). Related sessions are cleaned up automatically |

### Serial input and idle close

Both options in **Bot settings** are set per group × bot. Both are off by default and take effect after saving, with no restart.

| Setting | What it does when on |
|---|---|
| Process group messages in order | While the bot is working on a turn, new messages in the group (your own included) wait in a queue. Once the turn is done they are handled one by one in arrival order, without interrupting the current turn. Applies only to messages received after saving, and is independent of Oncall. Sessions taken over with `/adopt` are not affected |
| Automatically close inactive sessions | Sessions in this group (existing and new) are closed automatically once no new message has arrived for the chosen duration. The duration is a positive whole number in **Days** or **Hours**, 1 day by default |

Auto-close only closes sessions that are idle or dormant. These are skipped:

* Sessions that are running, waiting for you to confirm or pick a repo, flagged as needing you (including usage limits), or still have queued messages.
* Locked sessions.
* Sessions taken over with `/adopt`.

In a group where idle close was never set, sessions are not closed for being idle.

## Bot Config

Each bot's default behavior lives here, in five categories: Common / Sessions / Security / Message cards / Advanced. Switching categories keeps unsaved input.

A few frequently used items:

* **Default Role**: the bot's default persona in every session; a single group can override it in Role Management.
* **Blocked users (`blockedUsers`)**: people on this list cannot trigger the bot.
* **Quiet mode preset**: one click turns off thinking cards, turns on silent emoji reactions, and turns off streaming cards. It is a one-time write; changing those three switches later is not affected.
* **Card Signature**: a personal signature in the footer of final-answer cards.

### Rename, avatar, and profile description

At the top of the Bot Config page you can change the bot's name, avatar, and Feishu profile description. Saving syncs to the Feishu Open Platform and publishes a new app version, which takes about 10 seconds. After that the group shows the new name and avatar.

This step uses the Feishu web login cached on the server. When that login is missing or expired, the page says so and shows a **Scan to log in to Feishu** button:

1. Click **Scan to log in to Feishu** to show a QR code.
2. Scan it with the Feishu app and confirm the login.
3. After a successful login, the rename or avatar change is retried automatically. The profile description is reloaded, and you need to click **Publish descriptions** again for your draft.

The login is stored only on this machine and is shared with `botmux setup`. The account you scan with must be a collaborator on the app, or you get a no-access warning. If the rename fails on the Feishu side, only the Dashboard display name is updated. International Lark tenants do not support automatic changes to the name, avatar, or description yet.

## Data Insights

Data Insights analyzes the tool calls (spans) in your sessions to show what is slow and what keeps failing. At the top you can filter by project, time (all time, or the last 1 / 7 / 30 days), and CLI, or narrow to sessions that are **Worth review**, **Has failures**, or **Has slow spans**.

| Tab | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| Overview | How are things overall: sessions, spans, failed spans, slow spans, read/write ratio, plus the top suggestions and the tools that fail most |
| Sessions | What did one session do: sort by recent, review score, failures, duration, and more; open one to see its action spans, subagents, and suggestions |
| Flow | Where does the time go: action count and time share for the research, edit, run, delegate, and discuss phases, plus each session's rhythm |
| Distribution | What is typical: per-session distributions of spans, failures, slow spans, agent time, read/write ratio, and lines changed, plus daily session counts for the last 4 weeks |
| Hotspots | What keeps coming back: files, commands, and errors that recur across sessions, the project breakdown, and the slowest sessions |

Durations count only tool execution time and leave out time spent waiting for your reply, so they are not wall-clock time. CLIs are measured differently (for example Codex reads files mostly through the shell, so its read/write ratio runs low), so cross-CLI comparisons are only a rough guide.

## Workflows

The workflow feature is off by default. To use it, first turn on **Enable the workflow feature** under **Global Settings → General → Workflow**.

* **Run list**: every workflow run and its status. With no runs yet, start one in Lark with `/workflow new`.
* **Run detail**: the node graph shows which bot owns each node, its current status, and how long it took; click a node for dependencies, placement, its instance terminal, and more.
* **Cancel run**: finished nodes are kept; running nodes are interrupted.

Two things are not done in the Dashboard:

* Human approval in a workflow (humanGate approve / reject) happens on a **Lark approval card**.
* Triggering a workflow with parameters goes through [Connectors (Webhook)](/botmux/en/webhook.md).

## Monitoring Board and Session Monitor Room {#monitoring}

There by default, and visible in read-only mode too: **Analytics → Monitoring Board** in the sidebar (`#/monitoring`) shows botmux's runtime health on this machine (is the data fresh, is the daemon online, are sessions piling up), memory use and session pressure in real time. Memory is counted as PSS (`phys_footprint` on macOS) and split into botmux itself and external CLIs, so adding up processes doesn't double-count shared memory.

To watch several sessions' terminals at once: select them in **Session Control**, click **Add to monitor room**, and they appear side by side in the **Session Monitor Room** (`#/monitor-room`).

## Agents and the links graph {#agents}

There by default, login required: **Digital Workforce → Agents** in the sidebar (`#/agents`). An Agent is a reusable run config (CLI, model, working directory, sandbox). One Agent can back many bots, and an edit syncs to new sessions of every linked bot.

1. Click **New Agent** and start from **Copy from a Bot** (identical to that bot's config; you can tick **Also link this Bot**) or **Blank**.
2. Switch between **Configure** and **Links** at the top of the page. In **Links**, drag from the dot on an Agent onto a bot to link them.
3. Once linked, the bot's run config is managed by the Agent; to change it on its own, unlink it in the links graph first.

Agents are optional: a single bot can still pick its CLI and model directly under **Bot Config → Common → Agent Config**.

## Customizing built-in prompts and skills {#customization}

There by default, login required: **Digital Workforce → Customization** in the sidebar (`#/customization`) lets you tune botmux's built-in framework prompt fragments and built-in skills. The page itself is in Chinese.

* Every entry can be rewritten; changes **apply from the next session, with no daemon restart**.
* Each entry can be reset on its own with **恢复出厂** (reset to factory), or all at once with **全部恢复出厂**. Every change stores a snapshot; **历史 / 回滚** (history / rollback) takes you back to any snapshot, and a rollback stores a snapshot too.
* **导出 bundle** (export) downloads your changes as a bundle; a teammate brings them in with **导入 bundle** (import; a snapshot is taken before importing).
* You can delete critical instructions (such as `botmux send`), but then the bot may be unable to post replies back to Lark; reset to factory if unsure.

## Host web terminal {#host-terminal}

There by default, **only for people who can manage this machine**: log in to the Dashboard with this machine's admin link, or open this machine's Dashboard from the central platform, and **Management → Terminal** (`#/terminal`) appears in the sidebar.

* **New shell** opens a login shell on this machine; you can also connect to existing tmux / herdr sessions on it from the list, including sessions botmux manages.
* Multiple tabs, full screen and font size are supported.
* Closing a shell tab ends that shell and anything still running in it; closing a tmux / herdr tab only disconnects and leaves the session alone.

It hands out a shell on this machine, which is a lot of power; don't share the admin link. This is not the same as the [web terminal](/botmux/en/web-terminal.md) on session cards, which only views and drives one session's CLI.

## Auto-start at boot

Under **Global Settings → System & Maintenance → Auto-start**, turn on **Start the botmux background service automatically** and botmux will come back by itself after a reboot or re-login. You must be logged in to see or change it.

The switch uses the same mechanism as the `botmux autostart` command. It only affects **the next boot** and does not start, stop, or restart the service that is running now.

## APIs for integrations

This part is for developers building monitors, status pages, or automation scripts. Everyday users can skip it.

### Rename a group

An authenticated integration can rename a Lark group as a specific bot:

```http
PUT /api/groups/{chatId}/name/{larkAppId}
Content-Type: application/json

{"name":"New group name"}
```

* URL-encode both path segments.
* The chosen bot must currently be in the group; on failure botmux does **not** retry with another bot.
* The name is at most 100 characters (Unicode code points) and may not contain control or invisible formatting characters.
* The request body is at most 4 KiB and accepts only `name`.
* Dashboard management rights are required; even with public read-only on, this write can never be anonymous.

### Read-only query endpoints

| Endpoint | Contents |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/dashboard/v1/summary` | A versioned, strongly redacted overall summary |
| `GET /api/sessions` | All current active + closed sessions |
| `GET /events` | The Dashboard's external SSE stream. `session.spawned` carries the full session in `body.session`; `session.update` carries changed fields in `body.patch` |

Each daemon also has a `/api/events` endpoint that listens only on loopback. It is the internal channel the Dashboard uses to aggregate data, not an external address.

### Summary `GET /api/dashboard/v1/summary`

Use it to plug botmux into an external status page, monitor, or orchestrator. It aggregates sessions and scheduled tasks from online daemons and returns only allow-listed statuses and counts. It **never** returns bot / session IDs, titles, group names, working directories, prompts, scheduled-task contents, or diagnostic logs. The 200, 429, and 503 responses all carry `Cache-Control: no-store`.

:::tip
This endpoint is served by the `botmux-dashboard` process that `botmux start` launches. `botmux serve --api-only` does not start the Dashboard, so the endpoint does not exist there; see [Core-only API Control](/botmux/en/api-core-only.md) for that mode's health check.
:::

Success returns HTTP 200. Note that 200 only means the snapshot was generated: when a configured bot is offline, `service.status` is still `degraded`.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "generatedAt": "2026-08-09T02:30:00.000Z",
  "service": { "status": "healthy" },
  "bots": { "online": 3 },
  "sessions": { "active": 7, "attention": 1 },
  "schedules": {
    "enabled": 2,
    "nextRunAt": "2026-08-09T04:00:00.000Z"
  },
  "dashboard": { "href": "/" }
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `schemaVersion` | Version of the response format; currently `1` |
| `generatedAt` | When this snapshot was generated (ISO-8601) |
| `service.status` | `healthy` when the online bot count equals the configured bot count, otherwise `degraded` |
| `bots.online` | Number of daemons / bots online now |
| `sessions.active` | Sessions on online daemons whose status is not `closed` |
| `sessions.attention` | Active sessions that need a person: waiting for a repo choice, a TUI prompt, an agent asking for attention, or the `limited` / `stalled` states |
| `schedules.enabled` | Enabled scheduled tasks on online daemons |
| `schedules.nextRunAt` | Earliest next-run time among enabled scheduled tasks (ISO-8601), or `null` if none |
| `dashboard.href` | Relative path to the Dashboard home; resolve it against the current Dashboard address |

If any online daemon's data times out, errors, or is malformed, the endpoint returns HTTP 503 and **deliberately leaves out the counts**, so "could not read" is never mistaken for "zero":

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "generatedAt": "2026-08-09T02:30:00.000Z",
  "service": { "status": "degraded" }
}
```

**Anonymous rate limit**: requests without a valid token share one quota, at most 5 in any 10 seconds. The sixth returns HTTP 429:

```json
{
  "error": "rate_limited",
  "retryAfterSeconds": 7
}
```

The `Retry-After` header carries the same number of seconds (at least `1`, normally `1`–`10`); wait that long before retrying.

Requests with the current token are not rate limited. Authentication works like the browser login: visiting with `?t=<token>` first returns a 302, sets the `botmux_dashboard_token` cookie, and redirects to the address without the query. A pure API client that wants to skip the limit must keep this cookie and send it on later requests. `Authorization: Bearer` is **not** supported here.

### Optional fields in session data

These fields only appear in session data from `/api/sessions` and `/events`; the summary endpoint never returns them. They are all **optional**: older sessions or versions may omit them, so handle their absence:

| Field | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `backendType` | The backend used at the latest launch (`pty` / `tmux` / `herdr` / `zellij` / `zmx`), for filtering and display; it may change after a cold resume if the config changed |
| `backendSessionName` | Present only for managed persistent-backend sessions; currently `bmx-<first 8 chars of sessionId>`. PTY sessions, adopted sessions, and some old rows lack it. It is locator information only and **does not mean the process or socket is still alive** |
| `titleUpdatedAt` | When the title was last updated (ISO-8601) |
| `titleSource` | Where the title came from: `initial` / `user` / `agent` / `cli` / `dashboard` / `system`. For display and debugging only, **not usable as identity or audit evidence** |

### Public read-only and the token boundary

Public read-only (`publicReadOnly`) is on by default. While it is on, these read endpoints are reachable on the Dashboard listener **without a token**:

* `GET /api/dashboard/v1/summary` (strongly redacted summary)
* `GET /api/sessions` (session list)
* `GET /api/schedules` (scheduled tasks; prompts are hidden for anonymous callers)
* `GET /api/settings` (read-only settings)
* `GET /api/groups` (bot names and group names)
* `GET /events` (event stream; scheduled-task prompts are hidden for anonymous callers)

So treat session names, titles, backend types, and other session metadata as "public to this network".

* All writes (POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE), read endpoints not on the list above, and raw terminal output and diagnostic logs always need the current token. The list is "private by default": a read endpoint added later does not become public just because public read-only is on.
* With public read-only off, a tokenless summary request returns 401; a request with the current token still works and is not rate limited. With public read-only on, a wrong or rotated old token is treated as anonymous.
* The token only controls access at the Dashboard application layer; it does not replace a host firewall, VPN, or reverse-proxy authentication.
* If you do not need anonymous viewing, turn off **Allow tokenless read-only dashboard access** under **Global Settings → General → Access**. You can also set `BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_PUBLIC_READONLY=false` before starting; but once the switch has been saved on the settings page, the value in `~/.botmux/config.json` wins over the environment variable.

## Deployment details

The Dashboard is a separate process, `botmux-dashboard`, managed by the built-in supervisor; it starts and stops together with the daemon.

Each daemon exposes its internal API only on `127.0.0.1`. The Dashboard process forwards requests and checks signatures. The signing key lives in `~/.botmux/.dashboard-secret` (mode 0600), is used only between the daemon and the Dashboard, and is **never sent to the browser**; the browser uses the login token described above.



---
url: /botmux/en/decision-board.md
---

# Decision Board and Steward

Make one bot your **steward**: you hand it development tasks and it pushes them forward in the relevant chats. Anything that needs your call goes onto the **decision board**. You write a decision per item (screenshots welcome), click **Submit** once, and the whole batch reaches the steward as **one message**. The steward executes it item by item and writes the results back to the board.

```text
You hand a task to the steward ──▶ steward creates an item, pushes in the related chats
                                        │
                                        ▼  something needs your call
                              Board: "Needs you"
                                        │  you write a decision, paste images (auto-saved draft)
                                        ▼  click "Submit N decisions"
                              One message to the steward ──▶ executed item by item, written back
```

> Off by default. Bots without a steward get no extra files, pages or prompt text.

## Turn it on in three steps

1. Open Dashboard → **Bot Config** → pick the bot → the **Steward** section under the "Sessions" category.
2. Turn on **Make this bot a steward** and pick a chat under **Steward chat**. A regular chat with only you and the steward works best; a topic chat works too, but each batch is posted as a new topic.
3. A **Decision board** entry appears in the sidebar. From now on, just hand tasks to the steward in its chat.

With "Make this bot a steward" on but no chat picked, you can still read the board and write drafts, but submitted decisions have nowhere to go; the page tells you to pick a chat.

Settings in the Steward section:

| Setting | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Make this bot a steward | This bot's sessions can maintain the board with `botmux board` | Off |
| Steward chat | Where you hand out tasks; submitted decisions go to this chat's session | Not set |
| Decision cards in Feishu | See "Deciding on a Feishu card" below | On |
| Add the steward to new chats | See "Adding the steward to new chats" below | On |
| Also add it to chats with only you and one bot | Same | Off |
| Find items that are ready to close | See "Finding items that are ready to close" below | Off |
| Instructions | The built-in rules are shown read-only; **append** your own (e.g. your progress standard or the path to your merge standard) or **replace** them entirely | Append |

You can also use `/botconfig` in Feishu:

```text
/botconfig set steward {"enabled":true,"chatId":"oc_…"}
/botconfig set steward {"enabled":true,"chatId":"oc_…","guideMode":"append","guideText":"Progress standard: …"}
/botconfig set steward {"enabled":true,"chatId":"oc_…","decisionCards":false}   # no decision cards
/botconfig unset steward          # turn the steward off; board data is kept
```

`guideMode` is `append` (after the built-in rules) or `replace` (replace them; `guideText` is then required).

## How the steward works

* **Rules on demand**: each turn in the steward chat carries just one extra system line pointing at the board and at `botmux board guide`. The rules themselves are not kept in context.
* **Posts as itself**: by default the steward posts in other chats as its own bot (`botmux send`). Target bots must receive its messages: enable "receive messages that @ this bot from other bots" in the Feishu developer console, and grant the steward bot talk permission in botmux.
* **Hands you the hard calls**: anything it cannot decide, or anything irreversible, becomes a "needs decision" item with two or three options, their consequences and its recommendation. Without a progress standard it only reports and nudges; it never merges, closes, releases, deploys or deletes on your behalf.
* **Not a workflow node**: a bot with the steward on is never assigned [workflow](/botmux/en/workflow.md) nodes and cannot be the orchestrator bot.

### Scheduled patrol

Want the steward to check in regularly → tell it in its chat, for example, "patrol every day at 9:30". It creates a silent [scheduled task](/botmux/en/schedule.md) in the steward chat. Each patrol:

1. **Wraps up**: checks unfinished board items against reality, closes what is done, updates what changed.
2. **Discovers**: looks at the owner's open PRs and new activity in linked chats from the last 7 days, and writes what needs your call as decision items.
3. **Reports only what is new**: it only flags new decision items; with nothing new it stays quiet.

The rules are the "Scheduled patrol" section of `botmux board guide`; change them (for example the time window) in the custom prompt. Use `botmux schedule` to change the frequency, pause or delete it.

`botmux board add` with an existing dedupe key (`--key`) updates that item, but it is refused when the item is done or closed, so a patrol cannot bring old items back. To really reopen one, use `botmux board set`.

### Finding items that are ready to close

A PR merged long ago, or the work an item waited on is done, yet the board still says "In progress". Turn on **Steward → Find items that are ready to close** (or `"closeHints":true`) and the daemon checks the board every 5 minutes (no model calls):

| Situation | Mark on the board |
|---|---|
| All linked PRs are merged (the default when no close condition is set), or the `--close-when` condition holds | Suggest closing |
| Every item in `--depends-on` has ended, or the PR used to judge closing was closed without merging | Suggest moving on |
| The `--next-check` time has passed with no update to the item since | Check in |

* **Hints only, no state change**: the mark shows on the overview row and the item page, and one history entry is added. The steward verifies and changes the state itself.
* **Steward notice**: new hints from one run are combined into **one** message in the steward chat and sent to the steward session; each hint is sent once. A failed delivery is retried on the next run.
* **Dismissing**: changing the item's state, or `botmux board set <n> --dismiss-hint`, clears the hint; the same hint does not come back.
* **Items without conditions are untouched**: an item with no linked PR, dependencies or check time is ignored.
* PR checks use this machine's GitHub credentials (`GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN`, `~/.botmux/.env`, or `gh auth login`), and fall back to anonymous requests (60 per hour, shared by the whole machine). Open or closed PRs are checked at most every 10 minutes (a closed PR may be reopened, so it keeps being rechecked); only a merged PR is final and is not checked again. PRs that cannot be checked (not on GitHub, no access, rate limited) are left undecided for that run.

## Deciding on the board

### Overview

Three views: **Needs you** (including "needs review") / **In progress** / **All**, with search by title, repo or number at the top.

| Mark | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ● | The steward has new progress or a new reply since you last looked |
| ✎ | You have an unsubmitted draft |
| Open chat | Opens the item's main chat in Feishu; "+N more" under the title when there are several |
| No chat: (reason) | There really is no chat; the steward gave a reason |
| ⚠ No chat linked | Neither a chat nor a reason |
| 💡 Suggest closing / Suggest moving on / Check in | A hint from the board check (see "Finding items that are ready to close"), followed by the reason |

### Item page

From top to bottom:

* **Chats**: every chat of the item, main chat first and marked "Main", each with its own Open chat button; chats that could not be verified when linked are marked "Unverified".
* **Summary** and **current progress**.
* **Your decision is needed**: the question and options, with the steward's recommended option marked and its reasoning.
* **Your decision**: pick an option, write a note, paste or drop images (png / jpg / gif / webp, up to 10MB each, at most 8 per item).
* **History** timeline, plus linked PRs / sessions / commits.

**Previous / Next** at the top and under the decision box walk the list you came from (from "Needs you" they stay within it); opened straight from a Feishu link, they walk the view the item belongs to. Your draft is saved before switching.

### Drafts and submitting

* **Drafts are saved** on the server and never sent on their own. Your desktop and the Feishu sidebar share the same draft.
* If the steward changed the item after you started your draft, you get a "take another look before submitting" hint.
* Click **Submit N decisions** (on an item page: "Submit this decision" or "Submit (this + N other drafts)"). A dialog lists the drafts; unchecked ones stay as drafts.
* The checked drafts become one batch, delivered as **one turn** in the steward session; if the steward is busy, it queues behind the current turn.
* If delivery fails, "Recent submissions" shows why and offers **Deliver again**; undelivered batches are retried automatically after the daemon restarts.
* What you submitted is also posted verbatim in the steward chat: each item's number, title, main chat link, chosen option and your note, followed by the images. Long content is split across several messages, never cut.

### Deciding on a Feishu card

When the steward turns an item into a decision item or changes its options, a decision card for that item appears in the steward chat, so you can decide without opening the board:

* The card shows the title, a one-line status and the question, with one button per option; the steward's recommendation is marked and highlighted. Type a note in the box above to send it along with the option, or click **Send note only**. **Open in board** is at the bottom.
* Only you (the owner of the steward bot) can click; anyone else gets a no-permission message.
* A click works like submitting on the board: the item goes to the steward as its own batch and shows up in the timeline and "Recent submissions". The card switches to "Picked X, sending to the steward" and then "sent to the steward"; if delivery fails it shows why, and you can deliver it again on the board or click the same option again.
* Each item has one card. Later changes (new options, a web submission, the steward handling it, the item closing) update that card in place instead of posting a new one.
* When both the card and the web page submit for the same item, **the later one wins**, and the card says which batch it superseded or was superseded by. If the earlier batch has not reached the steward yet, it is voided and no longer pending. If it already reached the steward, which may be working on it, it stays pending, and the new batch tells the steward to mark that one as it actually went before acting on the new decision. Consecutive web submissions still run batch by batch as before.
* A web draft written before the steward changed the options (the chosen option is gone), or for an item no longer awaiting a decision, is still delivered when submitted, but does not supersede the card decision.
* With more than 6 options, content too long for a card, or an item that no longer awaits a decision (including closed or done), the card only shows the status and the board link.

To turn cards off, switch off **Decision cards in Feishu** in the Steward section of the bot settings. It only applies to bots with the steward on and a steward chat picked; other chats are unaffected.

### States

There are six: needs decision, needs review, in progress, waiting, done, closed. Finer workflow words (in review, fixing, mergeable, waiting on author …) go into the free-text stage.

## Chats linked to items

Every item links the Feishu chat where the work happens, so the board can take you there in one click.

* **New items need a chat**: `botmux board add` is rejected without `--link chat=oc_…`. If there really is no chat (only an issue, not started, or the steward handles it itself), give the reason with `--no-chat "<reason>"`; adding a chat later clears it. `board set` does not enforce this and existing items are not migrated; `board list` marks items with neither a chat nor a reason as missing a chat so the steward can fill them in.
* **Chats are verified when linked**: the steward bot's daemon looks the chat up with the credentials of bots on this machine. The steward bot goes first, then the other bots in turn (only those with the same owner, same brand and Feishu credentials; on a machine shared by several people, other people's bots are never used; if the steward does not trust same-owner bots on this machine, only the steward itself is used).
  * Found: the chat name becomes the default label (a label given by the steward wins).
  * Not found by any bot: the write is rejected, listing each bot's reason. To write it anyway, add `--allow-unverified-chat`; the board marks it "Unverified".
  * Credentials are only used inside the daemon process on this machine; they are never stored or printed.
  * Linking an existing chat again re-verifies it: the chat name and verification status are refreshed, the steward's own label is left alone. Older links can get their name filled in this way.
* **Main chat**: with several chats (a task chat plus some PR review chats) the first one is the main chat, opened by the overview's Open chat button; change it with `--primary-chat oc_…`.

## Adding the steward to new chats

To post in a chat as itself, the steward has to be a member. So once a steward is on, whenever botmux creates a chat (`/group`, the session chat created from a direct message, `/fork --create`, `/relay --create`, Dashboard group creation, `botmux create-group` and every other entry point) and the steward's owner is a member or the initiator, the creating bot adds the steward too.

* **On by default.** If you do not need it (for example the steward posts as the owner instead), turn off **Steward → Add the steward to new chats**, or run `/botconfig set steward {"enabled":true,"chatId":"oc_…","autoJoinNewGroups":false}`.
* **Joins quietly**: the steward does not speak or start a session. Its group-join command, group-join hooks and "auto-start when added to a new chat" do not run, it does not pull its owner in, and it is left out of oncall binding, role suites and kickoff. It answers later only when someone @-mentions it, as usual.
* **Only the matching steward**: when several people on one machine each have a steward, only the one whose owner is in the new chat is added. Owners are matched by union\_id; a steward with no owner (empty `allowedUsers`), or whose daemon has not resolved its owner's union\_id yet (just started, or no contacts permission), is not added.
* **One-person-one-bot chats are skipped by default**: for example the session chat created from a direct message, chats made with `/group` or `/fork --create` in a direct message, or meeting listener chats. You keep talking in those without an @; adding the steward would make it two bots, and the original bot would then need an @. This is decided from who actually joined. To add it anyway, turn on **Also add it to chats with only you and one bot** (requires the switch above), or set `"autoJoinSoloGroups":true`.
* A steward already among the requested bots is not added twice. If adding it fails (app visibility, permissions …) the chat is still created; the failure is logged, and Dashboard group creation and `botmux create-group` show the reason.

## Opening the board inside Feishu

Item links from the steward open in the **chat's right sidebar** on Feishu desktop and inside the Feishu client on mobile. Links carry no credentials; how you sign in depends on the deployment:

| Deployment | Sign-in after opening |
|---|---|
| Bound to the central platform with remote access on | Platform Feishu SSO; only the machine owner and co-managers get in |
| Dashboard Feishu H5 login configured (`BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_H5_*`) | Seamless in-Feishu login for listed users; H5 identities only gain the board APIs |
| Neither | The Dashboard login page; Feishu remembers it after you sign in once |

## Steward commands

The steward calls these itself inside its session; you normally do not type them. Knowing them helps when writing custom rules:

```bash
botmux board guide                                    # steward rules (built-in + custom)
botmux board pending                                  # submitted decisions not yet handled
botmux board list [--view decide|active|all]          # list items, each with a Feishu link
botmux board show <n|key>
botmux board add <title> --key pr:owner/repo#12 --link chat=oc_… --link pr=owner/repo#12
botmux board add <title> --no-chat "only an issue so far"            # no chat: say why
botmux board set <n> --link chat=oc_… --primary-chat oc_…            # add a chat / change the main chat
botmux board set <n> --state decide --ask "question" \
  --option "A=approach → outcome and risk" --option "B=…" --recommend A --reason "why"
botmux board set <n> --unlink doc=https://old --link "doc=https://new|Board doc"   # remove / replace a link
botmux board history <n> "what was done, result" --handled   # --handled: latest decision executed
botmux board attach <n> shot.png --note "repro"
botmux board set <n> --close-when "item:66 done" --depends-on 66,70 --next-check +2d   # when it can close
botmux board set <n> --dismiss-hint                   # dismiss the board hint
```

* `--link kind=ref|label`: everything after the last `|` is the label (write a literal `|` inside a URL as `%7C`).
* `--link` only appends; remove a wrong one with `set <n> --unlink kind=ref`.
* To write a chat that cannot be found, add `--allow-unverified-chat`.
* `--close-when`: `"pr:owner/repo#12 merged"`, `"item:66 done"`, `manual` (only the steward decides; linked PRs no longer trigger the default hint) or `auto` (remove it, back to the default). `--depends-on` replaces the whole list; `none` clears it. `--next-check` takes `+2h` / `+3d` / `+1w` or a time with a timezone (`2026-11-10T09:30+08:00`); `none` clears it.
* See `botmux board --help` for every option.

## Where the data lives

The board lives in `<data dir>/decision-board.sqlite` (one file per machine, partitioned per steward bot) with images under `<data dir>/decision-board/<app_id>/files/`, created on first use. Turning the steward off keeps the data.



---
url: /botmux/en/desktop.md
---

# macOS Desktop App

Botmux Desktop is the Mac app for botmux. It ships with its own runtime, so you **don't need Node or a global `botmux` command**. Double-click it to start the background service, browse the Dashboard, and read logs.

It's a good fit when:

* You run botmux on a Mac and want a window with start / stop buttons instead of remembering commands.
* You'd rather not deal with Node versions on your machine.
* You want botmux to start in the background when you log in to your Mac.

> For Linux servers or dev boxes, keep using the command-line install in [Quick Start](/botmux/en/quickstart.md). The desktop app is macOS only.

## How it relates to the CLI

| | Desktop app | CLI (curl / npm install) |
|---|---|---|
| Runtime | Bundled in the app, same version as the app | The `botmux` program you installed |
| Config, sessions, logs | All in `~/.botmux` | All in `~/.botmux` (**the same one**) |
| Bot processes | Started by the app's runtime | Started by `botmux start` |

Both sides read and write **the same `~/.botmux`**: bot config (`bots.json`), sessions, logs, and the background process records are shared. Moving from the CLI to the desktop app doesn't require reconfiguring your bots.

But **only one side can manage the bots at a time**. When the app opens it takes them over automatically; see [What happens when the app opens](#what-happens-when-the-app-opens).

## Install

1. Open [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/deepcoldy/botmux/releases) and find the latest stable release.
2. Download `Botmux-<version>-mac-universal.dmg` (or the `.zip` with the same name) from the assets.
   * It's a Universal build: works on both Intel and Apple silicon (M-series) Macs.
   * The package is signed and notarized by Apple, so macOS won't block it when you open it.
3. Open the DMG and drag **Botmux** into the Applications folder.
4. Launch Botmux from Applications or Launchpad.

> Only stable releases include the desktop package. Preview builds such as `-canary` or `-beta` are CLI only. The package is attached after the release is published, so it may not show up during the first few minutes.

**Before you start**: the AI CLIs you plan to use (such as `claude` or `codex`) still need to be installed and logged in from a terminal, and tmux is required by default. See [Prerequisites](/botmux/en/prerequisites.md). The app reads the PATH from your shell config (zsh / bash / fish profile and rc files), so any command your terminal can find, the app's bots can find too.

## First run

**You've used the CLI before**: just open the app. It picks up the bots already in `~/.botmux`, takes them over, and starts them.

**You've never configured a bot**: the bottom-left corner shows "Setup needed" and the dashboard can't load. Add your first bot first:

* Run `botmux setup` once from a terminal. A Feishu QR scan creates the app for you. This step needs the CLI installed first; see steps 1 and 2 of [Quick Start](/botmux/en/quickstart.md). Then go back to the app and click "Start".
* Or write `~/.botmux/bots.json` by hand following [bots.json](/botmux/en/bots-json.md) ("Open folder" in the app's top bar opens that directory).

Once the first bot exists and the service is running, you can add more bots with "Add bot" in the app's top bar.

## Everyday use

The app has three areas:

| Area | What it does |
|---|---|
| Left sidebar | Dashboard pages (Overview, Sessions, Groups, Schedules, Bot Profiles, etc.); at the bottom, the runtime status, "Start / Stop / Restart" buttons, and the "Launch app at login" switch |
| Top bar | Online daemons, items needing attention, configured bots; "Create session", "Add bot", "Docs", "Logs", "Open folder"; 中 / EN switch |
| Center | The embedded Dashboard, used exactly like in a browser; see [Dashboard](/botmux/en/dashboard.md) |

Common tasks:

| I want to… | Do this |
|---|---|
| Start / stop / restart all bots | The buttons in the bottom-left corner, or Start / Stop / Restart Botmux in the menu bar icon |
| Read logs | "Logs" in the top bar; pick a process in the drawer and copy with one click. "Open folder" opens `~/.botmux/logs` |
| Run automatically after logging in | Turn on "Launch app at login". The app starts quietly in the background and brings the bots up |
| Close the window | The red close button only **hides the window**; bots keep running. Click the menu bar icon to reopen it |

The menu bar icon's menu:

```
Show Console        Open the window
Start Botmux        Start
Stop Botmux         Stop
Restart Botmux      Restart
Open Logs           Open the logs folder
Open Botmux Home    Open ~/.botmux
Quit App            Quit the app
```

> "Quit App" only quits the app itself; it **does not stop the bots**. To stop them too, click "Stop" before quitting.

## What happens when the app opens

On launch, the app checks who is currently running the bots:

| Current state | What the app does |
|---|---|
| Nothing running | Starts them with the bundled runtime |
| Already run by the app | Nothing; it just shows the status |
| Started by the CLI `botmux start` (or a version different from the app's) | **Gracefully stops** those processes first, then brings them back up with the bundled runtime |

In the last case the bottom-left corner briefly shows a message saying it detected an external botmux runtime and is switching to the bundled one. This is a **normal handover**; your CLI install isn't being broken:

* Nothing in `~/.botmux` is deleted or changed.
* Like a regular `botmux restart`, sessions in progress are restored after the restart.
* Only botmux's own core processes are replaced; plugin services are left alone.

Also, **while the app is open**, if you run `botmux restart` / `botmux start` in a terminal, the app notices within a few seconds and takes the bots back. This keeps two versions from connecting to the same bots at once.

## Switching back to the CLI

To manage the bots with the `botmux` command in your terminal again:

1. Click "Stop" in the app (optional, but saves one restart).
2. Turn off "Launch app at login" so the app doesn't take over again at your next login.
3. Choose "Quit App" from the menu bar icon (or press ⌘Q).
4. In a terminal, run `botmux start` (if you stopped first) or `botmux restart` (if you didn't).

As long as the app isn't open, the CLI keeps managing the bots. If you open the app again later, it takes over using the rules above.

> If both autostarts are on (the app's "Launch app at login" and the CLI's `botmux autostart enable`), the CLI brings the bots up at login and then the app takes them over. It works, but costs an extra restart. Keep just one: if you use the app, run `botmux autostart disable`; if you use the CLI, turn off the app's switch.

## Upgrading

Download the new DMG, drag the new Botmux into Applications to replace the old one, and open the app.

When the app sees running processes from a different version, it restarts them once with the new version. Desktop upgrades follow the app only: `botmux update` or re-running the curl install script upgrades the CLI, not the app.

## FAQ

**The app keeps showing "Needs attention" and the dashboard won't load?**
Open "Logs" in the top bar first. Common causes: `~/.botmux/bots.json` is malformed (the bottom-left corner tells you which entry is wrong), or the app is still taking over from the CLI; wait a few seconds.

**Bots say they can't find `claude` / `codex`?**
The app uses the PATH from your shell config. First make sure `which claude` works in a freshly opened terminal. If you installed the CLI or changed your shell config after the app was opened: quit the app ("Quit App" in the menu bar), open it again, then click "Restart" so the bots pick up the new PATH. Reopening the app alone isn't enough, because quitting the app doesn't stop the running bots.

**The app quits right after opening?**
Usually the app bundle is incomplete (for example, an interrupted copy). Download the DMG again and reinstall over it.

**Bots still reply after I quit the app?**
That's expected. Quitting the app doesn't stop the service; click "Stop" first.

**Can I use the desktop app and the CLI together?**
You can keep both installed, and they share the same config, but only one runs the bots at a time. While the app is open, the app manages them; after you quit it, the CLI can. CLI commands that only look and don't change anything (such as `botmux status` or `botmux logs`) work any time.

url: /botmux/en/doc-comment.md
---

# Feishu Doc Comment Watching (/watch-comment)

Let the bot "live" in a Feishu/Lark cloud doc: ask a question or make a request in a doc comment, the AI reads the doc and does the work, then posts its answer straight back into **that comment's thread**. No need to leave the doc or switch to a group.

Good for:

* Asking "does this section match the code?" while reading a design doc
* Having the AI rewrite, extend, or review a passage in the doc
* Letting the AI pre-read a doc before a meeting, so everyone can ask in comments during the meeting

## Quickest start: @ the bot in a comment

No command needed. Open any Feishu doc the bot can access and `@the bot` in a comment with your question.

* When the bot picks it up, it adds a "Typing" reaction to your comment and removes it once the answer is posted.
* The answer is posted as the **bot's identity** in the original comment thread, and `@`s the person who asked.
* The doc is automatically registered as a "reply only when @ the bot" watch, so later `@bot` comments in the same doc are handled too.
* **Each comment thread in the doc gets its own session**, so conversations don't mix.

If the person mentioning the bot is not the bot owner, the bot still **replies right away**, but only after it manages to DM the owner a notice: who mentioned it, in which doc. If that notice can't be sent (or the bot has no owner configured), the bot doesn't reply and the auto-registration is undone. This is "notify, don't approve": the owner always knows, but replies don't wait for approval. To stop replying in a doc, the owner sends `/watch-comment off <doc link>`.

> This zero-command path relies on Feishu pushing the comment event to the bot. If the first mention gets no response, check "One-time setup" below, or register explicitly with `/watch-comment`.

## Bind to a topic: /watch-comment

To have comments share one AI session with a Feishu topic (for example, a topic already discussing this project), send this in that topic:

```
/watch-comment <Feishu doc link> [--dir <local project path>] [--all | --mentions-only | --owner-mentions]
```

After that:

1. If the topic has no AI session yet, one is created and the CLI starts right away;
2. The AI reads the doc first to build context, then waits for comments;
3. Matching comments in the doc are fed into this session, and answers go back to the original comment thread;
4. Status cards, terminal links, and other cards still go to this topic.

To answer with local code in mind, pass a project directory with `--dir`. Without it, the topic session's current working directory is used. If there is none, the AI answers from the doc alone, and the receipt reminds you that you can add one with `/cd <project dir>`.

> Every form of `/watch-comment` (register, `list`, `off`) is **bot-owner only**. Everyone else can only trigger replies by `@`-ing the bot in the doc.

### Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `/watch-comment <doc link> [--dir <path>] [mode]` | Register a watch and bind it to the current topic session |
| `/watch-comment list` | Inside a session: docs watched by this session. Without a session: all doc watches of this bot |
| `/watch-comment off <doc link>` | Stop watching this doc |
| `/watch-comment off` or `off all` | Stop every watch in the current scope (this session / this bot) |

Supports Feishu cloud docs (docx) and Wiki links.

## Which comments trigger: three modes

| Mode | Flag | Who triggers the AI | Good for |
|------|------|---------------------|----------|
| Only @ the bot (default) | `--mentions-only` | Comments that `@` the bot | Most docs, the quietest |
| Reply when the owner is @-ed (stand-in) | `--owner-mentions` | Comments that `@` the watch owner (whoever ran `/watch-comment`) or `@` the bot | Letting the bot answer questions people `@` you with |
| Every new comment | `--all` | Any new comment in the doc, no `@` needed | Bot-dedicated docs |

Notes:

* The stand-in and every-comment modes find new comments by **reading the comment list about every 5 seconds**, so there can be a few seconds of delay. Comments that really `@` the bot still arrive instantly, and the two paths never handle the same comment twice.
* When switching to one of those two modes, the bot only handles comments posted **afterwards**. It won't dig up old comments and answer them again.
* Auto-registration (the zero-command path) always uses "only @ the bot". To change the mode, run `/watch-comment <link> --all` (or another flag) again, or change it in the Dashboard. The Dashboard only offers "only @ the bot" and "every new comment"; the stand-in mode can only be set with the command.
* Use at most one mode flag. Passing several is an error.

### Set the default mode

The default mode for new watches is set per bot in **Dashboard → Bot Config** under "Doc subscription trigger (default)": "Only when a comment @s me" or "Every new comment".

The matching `bots.json` field is `docSubscribeDefaultMode`: `"all"` means every new comment; leave it out for only @ the bot.

### Pin a project directory to a doc

To have a doc always work in a fixed project directory, set `docRepoMap` in `bots.json`. Keys are doc tokens, values are absolute local paths:

```json
{
  "docRepoMap": {
    "<doc token>": "/home/me/my-repo"
  }
}
```

`docRepoMap` only applies to watches **not bound to a topic** (zero-command auto-registrations and watches registered in the Dashboard). A watch bound to a topic uses the topic session's working directory; to change it, use `--dir` or `/cd` in the topic.

## Manage it in the Dashboard

The Dashboard sidebar has a **"Doc watches"** page where you can manage everything without commands:

* **See the list**: every watched doc, its bot, working directory, and trigger mode;
* **See how it's running**: last activity, last delivery, total deliveries, and "why the latest comment wasn't answered";
* **Change mode / stop**: switch the trigger range right on the card ("only @ the bot" or "every new comment"), or click "Stop watching";
* **Register a new doc**: paste a doc link (or token), pick a bot and a trigger range, optionally fill in a working directory, then click "Start watching". A new doc isn't bound to any topic; a session is created when the first matching comment arrives. For a doc already bound to a topic, this only updates the mode and working directory, and comments still go back to that topic;
* **Spot the origin**: watches auto-created by someone else `@`-ing the bot are marked, so the owner can review them.

When comments fail to be handled, a "Document comment failures" panel appears at the top of the Dashboard overview and sessions pages. Expand it to see why, and jump to "Doc watches". In the doc itself, an `@` the bot couldn't handle also gets an error reaction, so the person asking knows to retry.

## What the AI sees

Each comment is handed to the AI together with:

* the doc link;
* for an inline comment (one made on selected text), the selected source text;
* earlier discussion in the same comment thread.

When the question needs the full body, the AI is told to read the doc with an available Feishu doc tool first instead of guessing.

## How answers get back to the doc

* By default, the answer is posted as the **bot** in the original comment thread, with the first part `@`-ing the person who asked;
* Long answers are split into several comments automatically;
* A few comments (for example resolved ones, or docs whose settings block replies) can't take replies. The bot then **creates a new whole-doc comment** as the answer, so it always lands in the comment area;
* If the bot itself has no access to the doc, it falls back to posting as the authorized user. To keep answers showing as the bot, share the doc with the bot;
* Doc comments are a plain-text channel. Buttons, cards, and terminal links still go through the Feishu topic (doc sessions auto-created by the zero-command path post no cards and only reply in comments).

## One-time setup (Feishu Open Platform)

`/watch-comment` needs no User Token. The bot reads comments and posts replies with its app identity. You only need to do two things for the app in the **Feishu Open Platform console**:

1. **Permissions**: enable `docs:document.comment:read` (read comments) and `docs:document.comment:create` (post comments/replies), plus `wiki:wiki:readonly` for Wiki docs, then publish a version;
2. **Event subscriptions**: add the `drive.notice.comment_add_v1` (doc comment added) event, using long-connection delivery.

Once the bot has doc watches, its startup self-check verifies these permissions and DMs the admin if any are missing. Feishu can't auto-detect event subscriptions, so the self-check only reminds you to confirm it.

## Lifecycle

* `/close` on a topic session also removes the doc watches bound to it;
* After a daemon restart, watches and the reading progress of the every-comment / stand-in modes are restored automatically, without re-answering old comments;
* **A doc binds to only one session at a time**: running `/watch-comment` for the same doc in another topic moves it there, and the receipt tells you so;
* One session can watch several docs at once.

## Legacy command: /subscribe-lark-doc

`/subscribe-lark-doc` is the earlier approach, kept for those who need it. It requires a doc-scoped **User Token**, calls Feishu's per-file subscribe API, and binds the subscription to the current session. If the token is missing, the command gives you an authorization link; authorize and retry.

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `/subscribe-lark-doc <doc link>` | Subscribe to this doc with a User Token and bind it to the current session |
| `/subscribe-lark-doc list` | List docs subscribed by this session |
| `/subscribe-lark-doc off` | Unsubscribe all docs of this session |

Prefer `/watch-comment` for new setups. You only need `/subscribe-lark-doc` when the zero-command path receives no events and you want to force Feishu's per-file subscription. Docs subscribed this way are unsubscribed through the Feishu API on `/close`.
