url: /botmux/en/env.md
---

# Environment Variables and File Locations

Most settings live in `bots.json` and the Dashboard, so **you usually don't need environment variables**. Only a few machine-wide switches (bind address, ports, external address, backend type, and so on) go in `~/.botmux/.env`. This page lists those switches and where botmux keeps its key files, for backup and troubleshooting.

**When to read this page**: the Dashboard or web terminal won't open, you need to change a bind address or port, terminal links show the wrong address, you want the pty backend, or you're looking for config / logs / data.

> This page covers **botmux's own processes**. To control which variables the CLI inside a session receives, use the Dashboard: "Settings → Session environment" (global) or "Bot settings → Advanced → Startup environment → Session environment" (per bot). See [bots.json → Session environment](/botmux/en/bots-json.md#session-env).

## How to change a setting

1. Edit `~/.botmux/.env`, one `KEY=value` per line:

   ```bash
   # ~/.botmux/.env
   WEB_EXTERNAL_HOST=10.0.0.12
   BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_PORT=7891
   ```

2. Restart to apply:

   ```bash
   botmux restart
   ```

**Put values in the file instead of only `export`ing them in a shell.** A restart that a bot runs from inside a Feishu session reads only `~/.botmux/.env` and does not inherit your shell. A value you only exported is lost on the next in-session restart.

## Network and access addresses

These decide whether other people can open web terminal and Dashboard links.

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|------|------|------|
| `WEB_HOST` | `0.0.0.0` | Address the web terminal service listens on |
| `WEB_EXTERNAL_HOST` | Local LAN IP, auto-detected | Hostname / IP used in terminal links on cards. Set it when the machine has several NICs or you access it by domain (see [Web Terminal](/botmux/en/web-terminal.md)) |
| `BOTMUX_WEB_PROXY_BASE_PORT` | `8800` | Each bot's terminal entry port = this value + bot index (bot 1 is 8800, bot 2 is 8801, …) |
| `WEB_EXTERNAL_PORT` | Unset, uses the local port | Set when a relay host exposes a different port than the local one. Also offset per bot: the real port is `WEB_EXTERNAL_PORT + bot index` |
| `BOTMUX_WORKER_HTTP_HOST` | `0.0.0.0` | Listen address of each session's terminal sub-service (the old name `BOTMUX_WORKER_HOST` still works) |
| `BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_HOST` | `0.0.0.0` | Dashboard listen address |
| `BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_PORT` | `7891` | Dashboard port. If it's taken, botmux tries the next free port; the actual port is written to `~/.botmux/.dashboard-port` |
| `BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_EXTERNAL_HOST` | `WEB_EXTERNAL_HOST`, then a non-wildcard listen address, then the LAN IP | Hostname used when `botmux` commands print Dashboard links |
| `BOTMUX_PUBLIC_URL` | Unset | Set it when you put the Dashboard behind your own nginx (or similar) on one domain, e.g. `https://botmux.example.com`. Dashboard and card terminal links then become `<this URL>/…` and `<this URL>/s/<session ID>`, so you expose a single entry point instead of one port per bot |
| `BOTMUX_DEVBOX_AUTO_EXPORT` | On | On a Merlin Devbox, automatically creates a private short link for the Dashboard. Skipped when central-platform remote access or `BOTMUX_PUBLIC_URL` is configured. Set `0` or `false` to turn it off; on failure botmux falls back to the local address |
| `BOTMUX_DAEMON_IPC_BASE_PORT` | `7950` | Internal port used between bot background processes = this value + bot index, local-only. Rarely needs changing unless ports collide |

> Which address Dashboard links use: central platform (when remote access is on) > `BOTMUX_PUBLIC_URL` > Devbox short link > local `host:port`. Terminal links follow the same order, minus the Devbox short link.

## Dashboard access control

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|------|------|------|
| `BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_PUBLIC_READONLY` | `true` | Allows read-only browsing of the Dashboard (sessions, schedules, …) without a token, so stale links still work; writes still need a token. Set `false` to disable. **Note**: once you change this switch on the Dashboard "Settings" page, the value in `~/.botmux/config.json` wins and the environment variable no longer applies |
| `BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_TERMINAL_CONTROL_TTL_MS` | `300000` (5 minutes) | How long you can type after "taking over" a terminal in the Dashboard, between 10 seconds and 15 minutes. It returns to read-only on expiry, release, or disconnect |
| `BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_CONTROL_AUDIT_PATH` | `~/.botmux/audit/dashboard-control.ndjson` | Audit log for terminal takeover and similar actions. Records only time, user, session, and action, never typed input |

### Open the Dashboard from Feishu without logging in (optional)

Off by default. When on, you can open the Dashboard straight from a Feishu H5 app without a token in the link; only users on the allow list get in.

| Variable | Description |
|------|------|
| `BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_H5_ENABLED` | Set `true` to enable |
| `BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_H5_APP_ID` / `_APP_SECRET` | Credentials of the Feishu app used for login |
| `BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_H5_ALLOWED_OPEN_IDS` | Users allowed to sign in, comma-separated (open\_ids under that app) |
| `BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_H5_BRAND` | `feishu` (default) or `lark` |
| `BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_H5_ENTRY_PATH` | Login entry path, default `/auth/feishu` |
| `BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_H5_SESSION_TTL_MS` | Login lifetime, default 30 minutes, range 1 minute to 24 hours |
| `BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_H5_SECURE_COOKIE` | Set `true` when TLS terminates at an upstream proxy but `BOTMUX_PUBLIC_URL` isn't an `https://` URL |
| `BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_H5_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` | Number of reverse proxies in front of the Dashboard (default `0`, range 0–8), so rate limiting sees the real client IP |

These variables (including the app secret) are used only by the Dashboard process. Bot background processes and session CLIs never receive them.

## Sessions and behavior

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|------|------|------|
| `BACKEND_TYPE` | `tmux` | Session backend. tmux is always the default; if tmux is unavailable you get a card telling you so, and botmux does not silently switch to pty. Only an explicit `pty` selects the plain pty backend, and pty sessions don't survive a botmux restart (see [tmux backend](/botmux/en/tmux.md)) |
| `BOTMUX_FORWARD_FOLLOWUP_WAIT_MS` | `1500` | After a new topic is posted in a topic group, how long to wait for the same person's immediate follow-up so both go to the CLI together. `0` disables, max `10000` |
| `BOTMUX_SENDER_RESOLVE_TIMEOUT_MS` | `800` | Per-step timeout (ms) for looking up the sender's display name. Try `3000` on slow networks (at most 6 seconds if both steps time out). Owner identity checks keep their own 3-second budget |
| `BOTMUX_ASK_TIMEOUT_MS` | `86400000` (24 hours) | How long a CLI question turned into a Feishu card waits for an answer. After a timeout the question falls back to the terminal and can no longer be answered from Feishu, so the default is long on purpose. Shortening it is not recommended |
| `BOTMUX_PERMISSION_TIMEOUT_MS` | `600000` (10 minutes) | How long a tool-permission card waits. On timeout the request is denied and the session keeps going. Clamped to 1 second–14 minutes |
| `STUCK_DETECTOR_ENABLED` | On | When an input hasn't finished a turn for a while, checks whether the CLI is stuck on a Codex hook-review screen and warns you if so. Set `false` to disable |
| `STUCK_DETECTOR_TIMEOUT_MS` | `45000` | How long (ms) after an input the check above runs |
| `BOTMUX_SCHEDULE_TIMEZONE` | Unset: the timezone chosen on the page, else the host timezone | Timezone for [scheduled tasks](/botmux/en/schedule.md), e.g. `Asia/Shanghai`. Takes priority over the timezone chosen on the Global Settings page; invalid names are ignored |
| `BOTMUX_RECOVERY_FORK_BATCH` | `5` | When botmux restarts and recovers sessions, how many it relaunches per batch, so they don't all start at once and swamp the machine. Minimum `1` |
| `BOTMUX_RECOVERY_FORK_DELAY_MS` | `250` | Pause (ms) between recovery batches. Minimum `0` |
| `BOTMUX_WORKTREE_SLUG_AI_ENABLED` | Off | Set `true` to name new worktree branches with AI. See "Name worktrees with AI" below |
| `BOTMUX_ALLOW_UNKNOWN_SCOPES` | Unset | Set `1` to request Feishu scopes not yet in botmux's scope list (syntax check only). A stopgap when Feishu ships a new scope before a botmux release |
| `BOTMUX_CODEX_NODE_REPL_PATH` | Unset | Absolute path to an installed Codex `node_repl` executable, for opt-in browser features when no MCP runtime is configured |

`BOTMUX_ASK_TIMEOUT_MS` and `BOTMUX_PERMISSION_TIMEOUT_MS` are read by the CLI inside the session, which inherits them from `~/.botmux/.env` by default. Because they start with `BOTMUX`, they are botmux-reserved and can't be set per bot in the session environment. When a bot uses [strict process environment](/botmux/en/bots-json.md#strict-env), they don't reach the session and the defaults apply.

### Name worktrees with AI (optional)

Off by default. When botmux auto-names a new worktree branch (e.g. `/repo wt`), it uses a local naming rule. When on, it calls an OpenAI-compatible API you configure instead, and **sends the topic title / first message to that API**. When off, incomplete, or the request fails, the local rule is used.

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|------|------|------|
| `BOTMUX_WORKTREE_SLUG_AI_ENABLED` | Off | Set `true` to enable |
| `BOTMUX_WORKTREE_SLUG_AI_BASE_URL` | Unset | API base URL, required, e.g. `https://api.example.com/v1`. botmux appends `/chat/completions` |
| `BOTMUX_WORKTREE_SLUG_AI_API_KEY` | Unset | API key, required |
| `BOTMUX_WORKTREE_SLUG_AI_MODEL` | Unset | Model name, required |
| `BOTMUX_WORKTREE_SLUG_AI_TIMEOUT_MS` | `5000` | Request timeout (ms) |
| `BOTMUX_WORKTREE_SLUG_AI_EXTRA_HEADERS` | Unset | Extra request headers as a JSON string, e.g. `{"X-Team":"dev"}`. Ignored if not valid JSON |
| `BOTMUX_WORKTREE_SLUG_AI_EXTRA_BODY` | Unset | Extra request body fields as a JSON string. Ignored if not valid JSON |

### Host overload alert

Turn the overload alert on and pick the notification bot on the Dashboard "Global Settings" page (see [Global Settings](/botmux/en/global-settings.md)). The variables below fine-tune the thresholds; the enter thresholds take priority over the values on the page.

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|------|------|------|
| `BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_ALERT` | Unset | Set `0` to turn the overload alert off completely, whatever the page says |
| `BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_ENTER_LOAD_RATIO` | `1.5` | Overloaded when the 15-minute load average exceeds CPU count × this value |
| `BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_EXIT_LOAD_RATIO` | `1.0` | Recovered only once load drops to CPU count × this value or below |
| `BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_ENTER_MEM_FRAC` | `0.92` | Overloaded when the used-memory fraction (0–1) reaches this value |
| `BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_EXIT_MEM_FRAC` | `0.85` | Recovered only once the used-memory fraction drops to this value or below |
| `BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_MIN_REALERT_MS` | `900000` (15 minutes) | Minimum gap between two "entered overload" alerts |

Exit thresholds must be lower than enter thresholds. If one isn't, botmux sets it to 95% of the enter threshold and logs a warning.

## Paths, logs, and GitHub

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|------|------|------|
| `BOTS_CONFIG` | Unset, uses `~/.botmux/bots.json` | Use a different bots.json file |
| `SESSION_DATA_DIR` | `~/.botmux/data` | Where sessions, queues, and other data are stored. On startup botmux records the actual location in `~/.botmux/.data-dir` so command-line tools follow it |
| `BOTMUX_WORKFLOW_RUNS_DIR` | `~/.botmux/workflow-runs` | Workflow run records |
| `DEBUG` | Unset | Set `1` to enable debug logs |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | Unset | Token botmux uses for its own GitHub requests (Dashboard changelog, update checks, restart report) to avoid rate limits |
| `GH_TOKEN` | Unset | Same, used only when `GITHUB_TOKEN` is unset |

`GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN` are used only for botmux's own GitHub requests and **are not passed to session CLIs by default**. If a bot's sessions need one, add it to that bot's session environment.

## Advanced / special environments

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|------|------|------|
| `BOTMUX_COMPANION_SECRET_FILE` | Unset | Secret-file path for the [Local Companion API](/botmux/en/companion-api.md), usually set by `botmux start/restart --companion-secret-file`. Must be an absolute path to a non-empty regular file owned by the current user, mode `0600`, not a symlink. Never passed to session CLIs and never falls back to `.dashboard-secret` |
| `BOTMUX_COMPANION_BOT_APP_ID` | Unset | The single test bot bound to the Companion API, usually set by `--companion-bot`. Callers can't pick another bot |
| `BOTMUX_LOOPBACK_PEERS` | Empty | Only for unusual kernels that report same-machine connections as a LAN IP, causing Dashboard or internal calls to be rejected. Extra allowed source addresses, comma-separated IPs / CIDRs, e.g. `10.0.0.5,192.168.0.0/16` |

Notes on `BOTMUX_LOOPBACK_PEERS`:

* Empty by default: only `127.0.0.1` and `::1` are accepted, same as older versions.
* It relaxes only the "request must come from this machine" check. Signature, timestamp, and replay checks still apply, so a badly signed request is still rejected.
* Entries that are too broad (`/0`–`/7`) or malformed are ignored with a startup warning.
* Prefer a single address (`/32`) or the smallest real subnet. Write IPv4 addresses in IPv4 form: `10.0.0.0/8` covers both plain IPv4 and the dual-stack `::ffff:10.x` form.

## File locations

| Path | What it is |
|------|------|
| `~/.botmux/bots.json` | Bot configuration |
| `~/.botmux/.env` | The environment variables on this page |
| `~/.botmux/config.json` | Global settings saved from the Dashboard "Settings" page; see [Global Settings](/botmux/en/global-settings.md) |
| `~/.botmux/data/` | Session data, message queues, etc. (change with `SESSION_DATA_DIR`) |
| `~/.botmux/logs/` | Background process logs; also viewable with `botmux logs` |
| `~/.botmux/bin/botmux` | Entry script for the global `botmux` command (written automatically) |
| `~/.botmux/lark-scopes.json` | Full list of recommended Feishu scopes (written during setup; copy it into the open platform's bulk import) |
| `~/.botmux/.dashboard-port` | The port the Dashboard actually listens on |
| `~/.botmux/.dashboard-secret` | Dashboard signing secret (mode 0600, keep it private) |
| `~/.botmux/audit/` | Dashboard terminal-takeover audit log |

For backups, keep at least `bots.json`, `.env`, `config.json`, and `data/`.

url: /botmux/en/faq.md

# FAQ / Troubleshooting

> Collected from the README and frequent questions in the community group, and updated over time. For more pitfalls, see [Common Pitfalls](/botmux/en/pitfalls.md).

This page is grouped by topic:

| You want to fix | Go to |
|------|------|
| The bot doesn't reply, others can't use it, results never arrive | [The bot doesn't reply](#the-bot-doesnt-reply) |
| Grants, mention policy, adding the bot to groups | [Permissions and mentions](#permissions-and-mentions) |
| Restarts, suspending, interrupting, working directories, terminal won't load on a phone | [Sessions](#sessions) |
| Login errors, upgrades, fonts, wrappers | [Install and environment](#install-and-environment) |

## The bot doesn't reply

Match your **symptom** first — each one has a different cause:

| Symptom | Likely cause | Jump |
|------|-----------|------|
| **No reaction at all** (not even an emoji) | Event subscription, release, or long connection not working | [A. No messages at all](#a-no-messages-at-all) |
| Only **I (the owner)** can trigger it; others get an auth card or no reply | Others have no talk permission | [B. Others can't use it](#b-others-cant-use-it) |
| It **only replies when @-mentioned** and you want it to reply without @ | The group's mention policy | [B. Others can't use it](#b-others-cant-use-it) |
| The card says "working" and the terminal has output, but **nothing reaches Lark** | The model didn't call `botmux send` | [C. Terminal has output but nothing reached Lark](#c-terminal-has-output-but-nothing-reached-lark) |
| The session **won't start**, and the first message errors with `zsh: parse error` | The login shell's startup file switches shells | [Session does not start](#session-does-not-start) |

### A. No messages at all

Check in order (PersonalAgent comes configured; normally you don't need to touch this):

1. **Event subscription**: Open Platform → Events & Callbacks — subscribe to `im.message.receive_v1` and `card.action.trigger`, choose "Long connection (WebSocket)", and make sure the daemon is running.
2. **Bot capability**: Open Platform → App Features → Bot is enabled.
3. **Release**: the app must have a published version ("visible only to me" is approved automatically). After changing permissions or events you **must publish again** for them to take effect.
4. **Long connection taken**: make sure no other program is using the same app's long connection.
5. Once all of that checks out, run `botmux restart` from a clean shell.

> To have an agent investigate, see "General troubleshooting approach" in [Common Pitfalls](/botmux/en/pitfalls.md): use `botmux logs` to find the launch command and reproduce it locally, then check the real error in the web terminal.

### B. Others can't use it

botmux has two permission layers:

* **Talk permission**: who can talk to it.
* **Operate permission**: who can run management commands such as `/cd`, `/restart`, `/close`, and tap card buttons.

By default only people in `allowedUsers` can talk to it. Anyone else who @-mentions it is blocked, and the owner gets a grant request card. **Adding the bot to a group does not grant anyone access.**

| You want to | Do this |
|------|------|
| Let the whole group use it | Send `@bot /grant` in the group, or open the group's manage dialog in Dashboard **Group Management** and click **Whole-chat grant** |
| Let one person try it | `@bot /grant @someone` — 3 messages / 1 hour by default, adjustable on the card |
| Grant several people at once | Multi-select in the Dashboard group member list for a batch grant (up to 50 people) |
| Have it reply without an @ | Change the mention policy with `/mention-mode` — see [Why must I mention the bot in groups?](#why-must-i-mention-the-bot-in-groups) |
| Run duty Q\&A with one group per ticket | Use [On-Call Mode](/botmux/en/oncall.md) |
| Block someone | Add them to the blocklist `blockedUsers` in Dashboard **Bot Config**; they're blocked in groups and DMs, with no more request cards |

Full rules: [Permissions & Access](/botmux/en/permissions.md).

### C. Terminal has output but nothing reached Lark

Output printed in the terminal is not the same as a message sent to Lark. For CLIs that send explicitly (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity, CoCo, and others), the model must run `botmux send` for the group to see anything:

* Every send needs one of `--mention-back`, `--mention`, or `--no-mention`; otherwise it errors and sends nothing.
* If it only uses `echo` / `print`, or forgets `botmux send`, nothing goes out.
* Pass multi-line content with a heredoc; don't write `"line one\nline two"`.

Two cases where the model doesn't need to send by itself:

* **`codex-app`** (the Codex App protocol): botmux forwards the final reply automatically. Don't call `botmux send` for normal replies or they'll be posted twice; use it only for mid-turn progress, attachments, or @-mentioning another bot.
* **Zero prompt injection mode** (`promptInjection: "none"`): botmux picks the final answer from the CLI's transcript and posts it to Lark. See [bots.json](/botmux/en/bots-json.md).

## Permissions and mentions

### How are permissions divided? Who can operate the bot?

| Source | Grants | Notes |
|------|------|------|
| `allowedUsers` | Operate + talk | The owner and admins. Can run management commands, tap buttons, and change `/card` `/cot` `/mention-mode` |
| `allowedChatGroups` (`@bot /grant`) | Talk | Whole group, no quota, no expiry |
| On-call groups | Talk | Whole group, and the group is bound to a working directory |
| `chatGrants` / `globalGrants` (`/grant @someone`) | Talk | Per person, 3 messages / 1 hour by default |
| `blockedUsers` | Deny everything | Takes priority over every rule above |

Quotas, expiry, and request cards are covered in [Permissions & Access](/botmux/en/permissions.md).

### How do I let a whole group use it?

Send `@bot /grant` (same as `/grant all`) in the group:

* The group is added to `allowedChatGroups`, and everyone in it can talk right away — no message limit, no expiry.
* New members get access automatically; people who leave lose it.
* In a topic group it applies to the whole group, covering every topic.
* Revoke with `@bot /revoke`.

The group manage dialog in Dashboard **Group Management** also has a **Whole-chat grant** button. It grants talk only; operate permission stays with `allowedUsers`.

### How do I give someone a few trial messages?

Send `@bot /grant @someone`. The bot replies with a grant card that defaults to **3 messages / 1 hour per person**.

* To set the count directly: `@bot /grant @someone 20`.
* Duration options are 1 hour, 8 hours, 1 day, 7 days, and permanent; leave the quota empty for unlimited.

### What's the difference between on-call and `/grant`?

Both grant talk only, and neither has a quota. The difference is the working directory:

* `/oncall bind <dir>` binds the group to a directory, so new topics skip repo selection and start right away. Good for duty Q\&A.
* `/grant` only opens up talking and binds no directory. Good when group members ask questions in topics whose repo is already chosen.

### Why must I mention the bot in groups?

The default policy is `always`: in regular groups the bot replies only when explicitly @-mentioned, so bots don't talk over each other in groups with several bots or people. Send `/mention-mode` in the group to change it:

| Mode | Effect |
|------|------|
| `always` (default) | @ required |
| `topic` | No @ needed for replies inside its own topics |
| `never` | No @ needed anywhere in the group |
| `ambient` | No @ needed, but it stays quiet when someone else is named |

* Changing it requires operate permission and works in regular groups only.
* A "1 person + 1 bot" group needs no @ by default; you can turn that exception off with `soloGroupMentionBypass`.
* A few more exceptions exist (message listeners, no-@ commands, and so on). See [Mention Policy](/botmux/en/mention-mode.md) for the full list.

### How do multiple bots work together?

It works out of the box — add the bots to the same group:

* Just you and one bot: talk to it directly, no @ needed.
* A group with several bots or people: @ the bot you want to hand the work to.
* Bot-to-bot relays (say, one writes and another reviews): the bots @ each other; you only hand the work to the first one.

See [Multi-bot Collaboration](/botmux/en/multi-bot.md).

### Can I stop people from adding the bot to groups?

Not from botmux. "Who can add the bot to a group" is controlled by the Lark platform (app availability, who can add bots to groups). What you can do on the bot side:

* **Don't auto-start when added**: turn off **Auto-start when added to a new chat** (`autoStartOnGroupJoin`) under Dashboard **Bot Config → Proactive Start**. Even when it's on, the group must contain at least one person from `allowedUsers`.
* **Stay restricted**: being added is not a grant. People without access are blocked when they @ it, and the owner gets a request card.
* **Don't pull the owner into new groups**: by default, when the bot is added to a new group it also adds the owner (`autoInviteOwnerOnGroupAdd`). If an alert or on-call platform creates groups in bulk and the owner shouldn't be disturbed, turn off **Add the owner to chats the bot joins** under **Bot Config → Proactive Start**, send `/botconfig set autoInviteOwnerOnGroupAdd off`, or edit `bots.json`.

### Can a bot added to a new group read earlier chat history?

Yes. Tell it "look at the chat history", or quote a specific message. The Lark app needs its full permission set (including reading group messages).

### A regular group is too noisy — can I switch it to a topic group?

Yes, but the group owner or a group admin has to do it: Group Settings → Group Management → Message format → "Topic messages". The bot can't change group settings for you.

## Sessions

### Does restarting the daemon lose context?

Not with the default tmux backend. The CLI keeps running inside tmux, and after `botmux restart` the next message reattaches to the same process.

* Without tmux installed, botmux does **not** quietly fall back to pty; it shows a card asking you to install tmux first.
* pty is used only when you explicitly set `BACKEND_TYPE=pty` (or `backendType: "pty"` for one bot). pty sessions **don't survive a daemon restart** and have to be relaunched.

### What happens to work in progress when the CLI restarts mid-way?

When the CLI exits unexpectedly (a crash, the tmux server going away, and so on), botmux relaunches it with the previous context and reads the transcript the old process left behind to see whether work was cut off:

* **the previous turn hadn't finished**, such as a review half-way through;
* **background tasks died with the old process**, such as Claude Code background commands, Monitors, or background agents.

If so, the resumed CLI first gets a short note (it was just restarted, which background tasks were interrupted, check and continue), and one notice appears in the topic. Nothing is posted when nothing was interrupted.

* The same check runs on a cold resume after a suspend or a daemon restart; the note is placed in front of the next message to the CLI. CLIs that take the first message as a launch argument, such as Pi, only get the topic notice.
* Only the transcript is read, never the screen. This covers Claude Code, plus CLIs with structured transcripts such as Pi and Codex (for those, only whether the turn finished).

**Messages not yet handed to the CLI aren't lost:**

* A first message passed as a launch argument, where the CLI exited before starting on it, is typed in again after the restart.
* Messages still queued when the daemon restarts are delivered by the session's next worker.
* Messages older than 24 hours aren't re-delivered; the topic says they weren't delivered instead. The same happens when another restart interrupts re-delivery and delivery can't be confirmed.
* A message the CLI had already received and started on is not typed in again; the note above reminds it to continue. It is re-sent only when the restart has to open a new session without the old context.

### Does a session use memory forever if I don't close it?

No. Each bot has two automatic limits. A reclaimed session is "suspended": the CLI process exits and frees memory, but the topic stays, and the next message restores the context from disk (usually within a few seconds).

| Rule | Default | Where to change it |
|------|------|------|
| Max resident sessions: beyond this, the least recently used session is suspended | 30 | Dashboard **Bot Config → Resident session limit**, or `maxLiveWorkers` in `bots.json` |
| Idle auto-suspend: suspend after N minutes of continuous idle | Off | **Idle auto-suspend (minutes)** in the same place, or `idleSuspendMinutes` in `bots.json` |

* A session that is producing an answer is never interrupted.
* A session whose main turn has ended while background tasks keep running (the card shows "⏳ Main turn ended · background tasks running") isn't suspended either — suspending would kill those tasks, and they can't be brought back.
* Adopted external terminals and sessions that can't be resumed are exempt.

To clean up by hand:

| You want to | Command |
|------|------|
| Preview, then bulk-suspend sessions idle for 7 days | `botmux maintenance suspend-idle --older-than 7d --dry-run`, then replace `--dry-run` with `--yes` |
| Close one session | Send `/close` in the topic, or `botmux delete <id>` |
| Close all sessions | `botmux delete all`, or batch-close in the Dashboard |
| Clean up sessions whose process already exited | `botmux delete stopped` |

More commands: [CLI Commands](/botmux/en/cli-commands.md).

### Can I follow up or interrupt a running session?

By default it doesn't interrupt. New messages queue up and are entered in order after the current turn ends.

To stop and change course right away:

* Tap **⏹ Stop** on the card, or send `/stop` in the topic. It interrupts only the current turn; the session and its context stay.
* When the card shows the terminal screenshot, you can also tap the `Esc` or `^C` keys; in the web terminal you can press keys directly.

Then send your new request.

### Wrong working directory or repository?

* `workingDir` searches for git repos **downward** from that directory (up to 3 levels), never upward. Point it at a folder with many repos (such as `~/projects`) to list them all; point it at one repo to list only that repo (and its worktrees).
* Switch directories temporarily: `/cd <path>`.
* Skip the repo picker and go straight into one repo: set `defaultWorkingDir` (see side effects in [Common Pitfalls](/botmux/en/pitfalls.md)).
* Don't set `workingDir` to `~` — there are too many folders to scan.
* `/repo` numbers can change; use `/repo <project-name>` to pick a repo.

### Session does not start

Symptom: the session never starts, or the first message errors with `zsh: parse error near '\n'`.

Usually your login shell (`$SHELL`, often bash) has a "switch to another shell" line in its startup file. The classic one is in `~/.bashrc`:

```bash
if [ -t 1 ]; then exec zsh; fi   # common when chsh doesn't take effect
```

botmux starts the session inside tmux with `<$SHELL> -i -c '…start the CLI'`. `-i` loads that startup file, `exec zsh` replaces the shell, and the command that starts the CLI never runs — so the first message lands in an empty shell. botmux detects this and posts a diagnostic card instead of typing the message into the empty shell.

Pick one fix:

* **Set `launchShell` (recommended)**: start this bot directly with the target shell, skipping the startup file that switches shells.

  * In Lark, send `/botconfig set launchShell zsh`;
  * or fill it in under Dashboard **Bot Config → Launch shell**;
  * or add `"launchShell": "zsh"` to `bots.json`.

  PATH, nvm, and the like must live in the chosen shell's own startup file (such as `.zshrc`; for fish, `~/.config/fish/config.fish`).
* **Fix the startup file**: only switch when you open a terminal by hand: `[ -z "$BASH_EXECUTION_STRING" ] && [ -t 1 ] && exec zsh` (put PATH, nvm, etc. before this line).

Then run `botmux restart` and send another message. This only affects backends that start through a shell (`tmux` / `zellij` / `zmx`); the `pty` backend starts the CLI directly and isn't affected.

### The Workbench or terminal won't load on my phone?

If it works on your computer but on your phone the Workbench is blank or the terminal never shows up, open `<your Dashboard address>/workbench-doctor` in the phone's browser.

* This self-check page needs no sign-in. It checks the service version, sign-in state (cookies), the terminal link and the live connections on its own.
* When it finishes, send a screenshot to the bot or a maintainer. It shows whether the cause is the network, the sign-in state or a stale cache.
* The page never shows any token or secret, so the screenshot is safe to share.

For what each check means, see [Agent Workbench · Phone won't load it? Use the self-check page](/botmux/en/workbench.md#phone-wont-load-it-use-the-self-check-page).

## Install and environment

### How do I upgrade?

The safest way is to **re-run the install command**, no matter how you installed originally (npm / pnpm global installs included):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/deepcoldy/botmux/master/install.sh | sh
```

* It replaces `~/.botmux/bin/botmux` in place. The download is test-run on your machine first; if it can't run, the installer errors out and **keeps your current version**.
* You can run it again safely: it won't add PATH twice, and it doesn't need Node.
* Afterwards, **open a new terminal** and run `botmux restart`. The installer puts `~/.botmux/bin` at the front of PATH, and only a new terminal is guaranteed to pick up the new version.
* The `botmux` command inside sessions always matches the daemon version; no separate upgrade needed.

On v3.18.0 or later you can also use the built-in command:

| You want to | Command |
|------|------|
| Upgrade to the latest stable release | `botmux update` (`botmux upgrade` is the same) |
| Switch to a preview channel | `botmux update canary` (`beta`, `rc`, `next` also work) |
| Install a specific version | `botmux update 3.28.0` |

Install a specific version with curl (same for rollback or pinning; the tag needs the `v`):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/deepcoldy/botmux/master/install.sh | BOTMUX_VERSION=v3.18.8 sh
```

> ⚠️ `BOTMUX_VERSION` must come right before the `sh` on the **right** of the pipe. If you write `BOTMUX_VERSION=… curl … | sh`, only curl sees the variable, `sh` doesn't, and you silently get the latest version.

#### Why can releases older than v3.18.0 only upgrade via curl?

From v3.18.0 the npm package switched from "Node + source" to **platform binaries**, and `node-pty` left the dependencies. Old releases' `botmux upgrade` handed the job to npm: crossing this version, npm deletes `node-pty` from the old directory, but the old daemon still loads it on restart, fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, and none of the bots come back (the output may already say "restarting to apply the update"). curl drops in the new binary without relying on the old directory, so it's the one safe way across this version. If you're not sure how you installed, just use curl.

### How do I fix `Please run /login · API Error: 403`?

First work out which side wants a login:

* **Lark authorization rejected** (calling Lark APIs as the user failed): send `/login` in the topic, open the authorization link, then copy the address the browser lands on (`http://127.0.0.1:9768/callback?...` — it's normal that the page doesn't load) back into the topic.
* **The model gateway returns 403**: unrelated to Lark; usually an environment variable or gateway token problem. A common cause is bash users putting variables in `.bash_profile`, which `bash -i` doesn't read (see [Common Pitfalls](/botmux/en/pitfalls.md)).

**claude keeps asking for `/login` on macOS**

claude stores its login token in two places, and the two drifting apart is the main reason for `Please run /login` on macOS:

| Where | Who uses it |
|------|------|
| Keychain item `Claude Code-credentials` | claude running in the GUI, and botmux's default (non-isolated) setup |
| File `~/.claude/.credentials.json` | Running `/login` over SSH can only write here |

As long as the keychain item exists, claude reads only the keychain, never the file. So "`/login` over SSH succeeded (it only wrote the file), but the GUI and the bot still use the old keychain token". On top of that, claude rotates the token on refresh, so whichever side refreshes first invalidates the other, and everyone gets logged out.

Stick to the file as the only source:

1. Don't use claude code in the GUI; it writes the token to the keychain.
2. Always update the token by running `/login` over SSH.
3. If an old keychain item already exists, delete it.

### `botmux history` returns 400, or the Lark gateway returns 411?

* **400**: usually the Lark app is missing a permission (such as `im:message.group_msg`). Enable the full permission list.
* **411**: older versions sent GET requests with an empty body, which the Lark gateway rejects. Upgrade to a newer version.

### Does it support Lark (international, larksuite.com)?

Yes. Both Feishu (feishu.cn) and Lark (larksuite.com) work:

* When you scan to create an app, China vs. international is **detected automatically**; when you paste the AppID / Secret by hand, you choose once.
* Each bot connects to the domain of its own edition. One machine can run Feishu and Lark bots side by side, with separate login credentials.

### Can I launch the CLI through ccr, a custom gateway, or a wrapper?

Yes. Write a wrapper script that passes its arguments (`"$@"`) straight through, then set `cliPathOverride` to that script's path when editing the bot in `botmux setup`.

### Chinese characters or emoji show up as boxes in screenshots?

Fonts are missing. On Debian / Ubuntu the daemon tries to install `fonts-noto-cjk` and `fonts-noto-color-emoji` automatically (needs root or passwordless sudo). On other Linux distributions, install Noto CJK and Noto Color Emoji by hand, then restart the daemon.

### A bot with `cliId: "gemini"` no longer starts?

Gemini CLI has been retired and the `gemini` adapter removed. That bot refuses to start with a hint to switch to Antigravity; other bots keep running. To migrate:

1. Install `agy` and sign in with a Google account (or set `modelProvider: "gemini"` in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` and provide `GEMINI_API_KEY`).
2. Change `cliId` to `"antigravity"` (in `bots.json` or with `botmux setup`).
3. Run `botmux restart`.

The old `cliPathOverride` / `wrapperCli` (such as `ttadk gemini`), Gemini `model` names, and `GEMINI_CLI_HOME` don't carry over. See [CLI Adapters](/botmux/en/adapters.md).

### Messages sent while CoCo is busy get lost?

Upgrade to **CoCo 0.120.32 or later**. Messages sent while it's busy go into CoCo's own queue, which relies on that version's behavior.

### Does it work on Windows?

Native Windows isn't supported: the daemon only runs on Unix-like systems, and there's no Windows build (neither curl nor npm can install one). Install inside **WSL2** and follow the Linux steps there.



---
url: /botmux/en/feedback-storage.md
---

# Feedback Storage & Migration

botmux keeps "feedback data" in a database: user ratings of final answers, the outcome of each turn, the delivery queue for feedback webhooks, and so on. This is what the Dashboard "Feedback analytics" page shows.

* **SQLite by default**: a local file, `botmux-feedback.sqlite`, in the botmux data directory (`~/.botmux/data/` by default). Nothing to install, and most people never need anything else.
* **PostgreSQL if you want it**: switch when you need central storage, backups, or to plug the data into your own analytics.

You switch storage with the `botmux feedback storage` command or with the "Feedback storage" panel on the Dashboard "Feedback analytics" page. Both can do the same things.

## Which should I pick?

| My situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| Fresh install, no special needs | Press Enter when the first `botmux start` asks about storage to keep SQLite |
| Fresh install, want PostgreSQL right away | Type `postgresql` at the first start, then give the config file path (see [Step 1](#step-1-prepare-a-config-file)) |
| On SQLite, **no feedback data yet** | [Empty database: enable directly](#no-existing-data-enable-directly) |
| On SQLite, **with history to keep** | [Migrate](#step-3-migrate) (needs a short downtime) |
| On PostgreSQL, want SQLite back or a different database | Not supported yet, see the [FAQ](#faq) |

> If the first start does not run in an interactive terminal (for example from a script), botmux uses SQLite without asking.

## Three things to know before migrating

1. **Service pauses during migration**: once the "maintenance window" starts, new topics, new turns, and `botmux send` are refused, and restarted daemons wait, until the migration completes or is cancelled. Pick a quiet time.
2. **No automatic fallback**: after switching to PostgreSQL, botmux will not switch back to SQLite on its own if the database fails. The old SQLite file is kept but marked "retired" and no longer written.
3. **Passwords never go on the command line or in the config file**: only "secret references" are allowed, see [How to supply the password](#how-to-supply-the-password).

## Switch from the command line

### Step 1: Prepare a config file

Create a JSON file, for example `pg.json`:

```json
{
  "backend": "postgresql",
  "postgres": {
    "host": "db.example.com",
    "port": 5432,
    "database": "botmux",
    "user": "botmux",
    "schema": "botmux_feedback",
    "passwordRef": "env:BOTMUX_FEEDBACK_PG_PASSWORD",
    "tls": { "mode": "verify-full" },
    "connectTimeoutMs": 5000
  }
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `host` / `port` / `database` / `user` | Connection details, all required |
| `schema` | A schema just for botmux. Pick a name that **does not exist yet** in the database; botmux creates it. Lowercase letters, digits, and underscores, not starting with a digit |
| `passwordRef` | A reference to the password, not the password itself (see below) |
| `tls.mode` | `verify-full`: verify the server certificate (recommended); `disable`: no encryption |
| `tls.caRef` | Optional reference to a custom CA certificate, same format as `passwordRef` |
| `connectTimeoutMs` | Connection timeout, 100–60000 ms |

Extra fields (such as a `password` key) are not allowed and the file will be rejected.

### Step 2: Save it as the candidate and test it

```bash
botmux feedback storage configure --config-file ./pg.json
botmux feedback storage test
botmux feedback storage status
```

* `configure` only saves it as the "candidate" config. **It does not switch and does not touch any data.**
* `test` connects to the database and checks that the account has the `CREATE` privilege on it (botmux needs it to create its own schema and tables).
* `status` shows the active storage (`active`), the candidate (`candidate`), and past migration jobs. Running `botmux feedback storage` with no subcommand also shows `status`.

All commands print JSON. On error they print `{"error":"feedback_..."}` and exit with code 1.

### Step 3: Migrate

```bash
botmux feedback storage migrate --to postgresql --yes
```

`--yes` confirms that you accept the maintenance window; without it the command is refused. The command runs until it finishes and prints something like:

```json
{"migrationId":"5dd49f52-...","phase":"complete","blockers":[]}
```

`phase: complete` means success (exit code 0), and feedback data now goes to PostgreSQL. Along the way it passes through these phases:

| Phase | What happens |
|---|---|
| `preflight` | Connect to the target and prepare the tables |
| `draining` | Enter the maintenance window and wait for running turns to finish (about 45 seconds max) |
| `snapshot` | Take a read-only snapshot of SQLite |
| `importing` | Import the snapshot into PostgreSQL (the target must be empty) |
| `verifying` | Compare row counts and contents table by table |
| `retiring` / `activating` | Retire SQLite and switch to PostgreSQL |
| `complete` | Done, the maintenance window ends |

If `phase` is `blocked`, the migration is stuck. See the next section.

### Stuck: resume or cancel

When `blocked`, `blockers` tells you why. **The maintenance window does not end on its own after a block**, so new turns stay blocked until you pick one:

```bash
# After fixing the problem, continue the same job (safe to repeat)
botmux feedback storage resume <migrationId>

# Give up and restore the original SQLite
botmux feedback storage cancel <migrationId> --yes \
  --reason "Target lacks permissions, retry later" \
  --evidence "ticket:1234"
```

* `cancel` needs `--yes`, `--reason` (why you cancel), and `--evidence` (what you checked, such as a ticket number). They are kept in an audit record.
* Cancelling only restores SQLite. **Data already written to PostgreSQL is not deleted.**
* Once SQLite has been marked retired (after the `retiring` phase finishes), you cannot cancel. Use `resume` to finish.

Common `blockers`:

| Reason | What to do |
|---|---|
| `feedback_maintenance_not_ready` | Not ready within 45 seconds: turns are still running, a `botmux send` is in progress or has an unknown outcome, or a daemon did not respond. Wait for turns to finish; acknowledge unknown sends via [Delivery recovery items](#delivery-recovery-items), then `resume` |
| `feedback_outbox_unsettled` | There are webhook deliveries with unknown outcomes. See [Delivery recovery items](#delivery-recovery-items), then `resume` |
| `feedback_storage_target_not_empty` / `feedback_migration_target_not_empty` | The target schema already exists and was not created by botmux, or it already holds feedback data. Use a schema name that does not exist yet |
| `feedback_storage_secret_missing` | The password reference cannot be read (env var not set or file missing) |
| `feedback_migration_database_or_io_error` | A database or disk error, most often the database is unreachable or permissions are missing. Run `test` to narrow it down, fix it, then `resume` |

### No existing data: enable directly

If SQLite has no feedback data yet, you can skip the migration:

```bash
botmux feedback storage configure --config-file ./pg.json
botmux feedback storage enable-empty --yes
```

If SQLite holds even one row, `enable-empty` refuses (`feedback_storage_migration_required`). Use `migrate` instead.

## How to supply the password

To keep passwords out of shell history and config files, the command line **rejects** `--password` and `--token`, and the config file only accepts references:

| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `env:NAME` | Read from an environment variable, such as `env:BOTMUX_FEEDBACK_PG_PASSWORD` |
| `file:<id>` | Read a protected secret file in the botmux data directory. Created automatically when you enter a password in the Dashboard; you rarely write it by hand |

With `env:`, the variable must exist **both** in the terminal where you run `botmux feedback storage` and in the environment of the botmux service itself, or the service cannot read the password after the switch. The simpler route is to type the password into the Dashboard panel: it is saved as a file readable only by the local user, the config keeps just a reference, and the page never shows it again.

## Switch from the Dashboard

Open the Dashboard "Feedback analytics" page and expand "Feedback storage". Only host admins can see this panel.

> The screenshot is from an earlier version. The current panel also has an "Authentication" dropdown next to "Backend".

<img src="/img/feedback-storage-panel.png" alt="Feedback storage panel: backend set to PostgreSQL, with host, port, database, user, schema, password and TLS fields, followed by save candidate, test saved connection, the maintenance confirmation checkbox and migration buttons" />

1. Set "Backend" to PostgreSQL and "Authentication" to "Username / password", then fill in the connection details. Leaving the password blank keeps the previously saved one.
2. Click "Save candidate settings", then "Test saved connection". The panel shows "Active: sqlite; Candidate: postgresql".
3. Tick "Confirm maintenance", then:
   * with history: click "Migrate and enable PostgreSQL";
   * with no data: click "Empty database: enable directly".
4. The migration runs in the background. The panel refreshes every few seconds and shows `<migration ID>: <phase> <reasons>` at the bottom. Settings are locked while it runs.
5. When it is `blocked`, a "Resume original migration" button appears (the confirmation box must be ticked). It does the same as `resume`.

To cancel, expand "Manual recovery and resolution" below, fill in "Reason" and "External verification evidence", keep the confirmation box above ticked, and click "Cancel migration and restore source". The button only appears while a migration is unfinished.

<img src="/img/feedback-storage-recovery.png" alt="Manual recovery and resolution section: reason and external verification evidence inputs, with buttons to cancel the migration and to list unknown deliveries and send leases" />

## Delivery recovery items

Before migrating, botmux must be sure nothing was "sent with an unknown result", or the data might not line up. There are two kinds:

| Kind | What it is |
|---|---|
| `webhook` | A delivery of a feedback webhook (`feedbackWebhooks` in the bot config) that went out without a clear result |
| `send` | A `botmux send` run whose process exited midway, so it is unknown whether the message went out |

List them:

```bash
botmux feedback storage recovery list
```

First check on the other side whether it actually arrived (for example the webhook receiver's logs, or whether the message is in the Feishu chat), then record your conclusion:

```bash
botmux feedback storage recovery acknowledge \
  --kind webhook --id <id> --fingerprint <fingerprint> --yes \
  --reason "Receiver logs show the event" --evidence "ticket:1234"
```

* Copy `--id` and `--fingerprint` from the `recovery list` output. If the item changed in the meantime you get `feedback_recovery_stale`; just list again.
* Items still in progress (`live: true`) cannot be acknowledged. Wait for them to end.
* Acknowledging only records your decision. It **does not resend** and does not end the maintenance window. Run `resume` afterwards.

On the Dashboard, the "List unknown deliveries and send leases" button in "Manual recovery and resolution" does the same thing, with an "Acknowledge verified outcome" button under each item (it also needs the confirmation box ticked and a reason and evidence filled in).

## Scripted installs

For automated deployments, set the environment variable `BOTMUX_FEEDBACK_CONFIG_FILE` to the config file from Step 1. `botmux start` then saves that config and enables it directly as an empty database (same as `enable-empty`), without asking. If the config matches the active one, nothing happens.

This is only for fresh installs: if SQLite already has data, it fails with `feedback_storage_migration_required`. [Migrate](#step-3-migrate) instead.

## FAQ

**Can I go from PostgreSQL back to SQLite, or to another PostgreSQL?**
Not yet. Migration only supports SQLite → PostgreSQL.

**How long is the downtime?**
It depends on the data size: running turns must finish, then the data is imported and verified table by table. With modest data it is usually quick. Do it off-peak.

**Is the old SQLite file still there afterwards?**
Yes. `botmux-feedback.sqlite` stays in the data directory, retired and no longer written.

**Getting `feedback_storage_generation_conflict`?**
The config was changed elsewhere while you were working (for example in an open Dashboard). Run `status` again and retry. You also get it if you run `enable-empty` without saving a candidate with `configure` first.

**Related pages**: [Bot config (bots.json)](/botmux/en/bots-json.md) covers the final-answer feedback card; [Dashboard](/botmux/en/dashboard.md) introduces the "Feedback analytics" page; other commands are in [CLI commands](/botmux/en/cli-commands.md).
